verses.1:1: And Solomon son of David became strong over his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and magnified him to great height.
verses.1:2: And Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of thousands and to the commanders of hundreds and to the judges and to all the rulers before Israel, the rulers of the ancestral houses.
verses.1:3: And Solomon and all the assembly went to the high place that was in Gibeon, where the tent of testimony of God was, which Moses, the servant of the Lord, made in the wilderness.
verses.1:4: However, David had brought up the ark of God from the city of Kiriath-jearim, because he had prepared a tent for it in Jerusalem.
verses.1:5: And the bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was there before the tent of the Lord, and Solomon and the assembly sought it out.
verses.1:6: And Solomon offered there on the bronze altar before the Lord, which was in the tent, and he offered on it a burnt offering of a thousand.
verses.1:7: In that night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what I should give you."
verses.1:8: And Solomon said to God, "What great mercy You showed with David my father, and You made me king in his place.
verses.1:9: And now, Lord God, let Your name be confirmed toward David my father, for You made me king over a numerous people, like the dust of the earth.
verses.1:10: Now give me wisdom and understanding, and I will go out before this people and come in; for who will judge this great people of Yours?"
verses.1:11: And God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for wealth of possessions nor glory nor the life of the adversaries, and you did not ask for many days, but asked for yourself wisdom and understanding so that you may judge My people over whom I made you king,
verses.1:12: wisdom and understanding I am giving you, and wealth and possessions and glory I will give you, such that there has not been anyone like you among the kings before you, and after you it will not be so."
verses.1:13: And Solomon came from Maba, which was in Gibeon, which was in Jerusalem, before the tent of testimony, and he reigned over Israel.
verses.1:14: And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen, and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen; and he left them in chariot cities, and the people were with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.1:15: And the king made gold and silver in Jerusalem like stones, and the cedars in Judea like the sycamore trees in the lowland in abundance.
verses.1:16: And the export of horsemen for Solomon was from Egypt, and the price of the king's merchants; they were buying to go.
verses.1:17: And they would go in and bring out from Egypt one chariot for six hundred in silver, and a horse for one hundred fifty; and in this way they brought them through their hands to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Syria.
verses.1:18: And Solomon gave word to build a house for the name of the Lord and a house for his kingdom.
verses.2:1: And Solomon gathered seventy thousand men and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain, and the overseers over them were three thousand six hundred.
verses.2:2: And Solomon sent to Hiram king of Tyre, saying, "As you dealt with my father David and sent him cedars to build a house for himself to live in,
verses.2:3: now look, I, his son, am building a house for the name of the Lord my God, to consecrate it to Him, to burn incense before Him, and for the continual presentation, and to offer burnt offerings continually in the morning and in the evening, and on the Sabbaths and on the new moons and on the festivals of the Lord our God; this is forever upon Israel.
verses.2:4: And the house that I am building is great, for our God is great above all the gods.
verses.2:5: And who will be able to build a house for Him? For heaven and the heaven of heaven do not bear His glory; and who am I, building a house for Him, except to burn incense before Him?
verses.2:6: And now send me a wise man who knows how to work in gold and in silver, in bronze and in iron, and in purple and in crimson, and who understands how to engrave an engraving, with the wise men who are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, which David my father prepared.
verses.2:7: And send me cedar, juniper, and pine timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut timber from Lebanon; and look, your servants with my servants
verses.2:8: will go to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house that I am building is great and glorious.
verses.2:9: And look, to the workers, those who cut timber, for food I have given wheat as gifts to your servants, twenty thousand kors, and twenty thousand kors of barley, and twenty thousand measures of wine."
verses.2:10: And Hiram king of Tyre spoke in writing and sent to Solomon, "Because the Lord loved His people, He gave you as king over them."
verses.2:11: And Hiram said, "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who gave David a wise son, versed in understanding and knowledge, who will build a house for the Lord and a house for his kingdom.
verses.2:12: And now I have sent you a wise man who knows understanding, Hiram my father.
verses.2:13: His mother is from the daughters of Dan, and his father is a Tyrian man; he knows how to work in gold and in silver and in bronze and in iron, in stones and timber, and to weave in purple and in blue and in fine linen and in crimson, and to engrave engravings, and to devise every design, whatever you may give him, with your wise men and the wise men of David my lord, your father.
verses.2:14: And now, the wheat and the barley and the oil and the wine that my lord spoke of, let him send to his servants.
verses.2:15: And we will cut timber from Lebanon according to all your need, and we will bring it on rafts to the sea of Joppa, and you will bring it to Jerusalem."
verses.2:16: And Solomon gathered all the men who were resident aliens in the land of Israel after the count with which David his father had counted them, and there were found one hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred.
verses.2:17: And he made from them seventy thousand burden-bearers, and eighty thousand stonecutters, and three thousand six hundred over the people.
verses.3:1: And Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the Lord had appeared to David his father, in the place that David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.3:2: And building began in the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
verses.3:3: And these things Solomon began, to build the house of God: the length in cubits, the first measurement, was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
verses.3:4: And the vestibule in front of the house: the length across the front of the width of the house was twenty cubits, and the height one hundred twenty cubits; and he overlaid it on the inside with pure gold.
verses.3:5: And the great house he paneled with cedar timber, and he overlaid it with pure gold, and he carved on it palm trees and hanging chains.
verses.3:6: And he adorned the house with precious stones for glory, and with gold of the gold from Parvaim.
verses.3:7: And he overlaid the house and the walls and the gateways and the ceilings and the doorways with gold, and he carved cherubim on the walls.
verses.3:8: And he made the house of the Holy of Holies: its length across the front, the width was twenty cubits, and the length was twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with pure gold for cherubim, for six hundred talents.
verses.3:9: And the weight of the nails: the weight of one was fifty shekels of gold; and he overlaid the upper room with gold.
verses.3:10: And he made in the house, the Holy of Holies, two cherubim, a work of wood, and he overlaid them with gold.
verses.3:11: And the wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits in length, and the one wing was five cubits, touching the wall of the house, and the other wing was five cubits, touching the wing of the other cherub.
verses.3:13: And the wings of the cherubim were spread out twenty cubits, and they were standing on their feet, and their faces were toward the house.
verses.3:14: And he made the veil of blue and purple and crimson and fine linen, and he wove cherubim into it.
verses.3:15: And he made in front of the wall two pillars, thirty-five cubits in height, and their capitals were five cubits.
verses.3:16: And he made chains in the inner sanctuary and put them on the capitals of the pillars, and he made one hundred pomegranates and placed them on the hanging chains.
verses.3:17: And he set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and the one on the left, and he called the name of the one on the right Establishment, and the name of the one on the left Strength.
verses.4:1: And he made the altar of bronze, twenty cubits in length, and the width twenty cubits; the height ten cubits.
verses.4:2: And he made the cast-metal sea, ten cubits in diameter, round all around, and five cubits in height, and the circumference thirty cubits.
verses.4:3: And a likeness of calves was underneath it; in a circle they encircle it, ten cubits encompass the basin all around; in two kinds they cast the calves in their casting,
verses.4:4: in which they made them twelve calves, three facing north, and three west, and three south, and three toward the east; and the sea was upon them above; their hindquarters were inward.
verses.4:5: And its thickness was a handbreadth, and its rim was like the rim of a cup, carved with buds of a lily, holding three thousand measures; and he finished.
verses.4:6: And he made ten basins, and placed five on the right and five on the left, to wash in them the works of the burnt offerings and to rinse in them; and the sea was for the priests to wash themselves in it.
verses.4:7: And he made the ten golden lampstands according to their ordinance and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.
verses.4:8: And he made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left; and he made one hundred golden bowls.
verses.4:9: And he made the court of the priests and the great court, and doors for the court, and their doorframes plated with bronze.
verses.4:10: And he placed the sea at the corner of the house on the right, toward the east, opposite.
verses.4:11: And Hiram made the meat-forks and the firepans and the grate of the altar and all its utensils. And Hiram finished doing all the work that he did for Solomon the king in the house of God,
verses.4:12: two pillars, and on them globes for the capital on the tops of the two pillars, and two networks to cover the tops of the capitals that are on the tops of the pillars,
verses.4:13: and four hundred golden bells for the two networks, and kinds of pomegranates on each network to cover the two globes of the capitals that are upon the pillars.
verses.4:14: And he made the ten stands, and he made the basins upon the stands,
verses.4:15: and the one sea, and the twelve calves underneath it,
verses.4:16: and the footed pots and the shovels and the cauldrons and the meat-forks, and all their utensils, which Hiram made of pure bronze and brought up to King Solomon in the house of the Lord.
verses.4:17: In the region around the Jordan the king cast them in the thickness of the earth, in the house of Succoth and Anamesirdathai.
verses.4:18: And Solomon made all these utensils in very great abundance, because the weight of the bronze did not fail.
verses.4:19: And Solomon made all the utensils of the house of the Lord, and the golden altar and the tables, and on them were loaves of presentation,
verses.4:20: and the lampstands and the lamps of light according to the ordinance and before the inner sanctuary, of pure gold,
verses.4:21: and their tongs and their lamps, and the bowls and the censers and the firepans, of pure gold,
verses.4:22: and the inner door of the house to the Holy of Holies, to the golden doors of the house of the temple. And all the work that Solomon did in the house of the Lord was finished.
verses.5:1: And Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father, the silver and the gold and the utensils; he put them into the treasury of the Lord.
verses.5:2: Then Solomon assembled the elders and all the rulers of the tribes, the leaders of the families of the sons of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the city of David, that is, Zion.
verses.5:3: And all Israel assembled to the king at the feast, that is, the seventh month.
verses.5:4: And all the elders of Israel came, and all the Levites took up the ark
verses.5:5: and the tent of testimony and all the holy utensils that were in the tent, and the priests and the Levites brought it up.
verses.5:6: And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel and those who feared and those of them who were gathered together were before the ark, sacrificing calves and sheep, which could not be counted and which could not be reckoned because of the abundance.
verses.5:7: And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the Lord to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, into the Holy of Holies, underneath the wings of the cherubim.
verses.5:8: And the cherubim had spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and over its poles from above,
verses.5:9: and the poles projected out, and the ends of the poles were seen from the holy place in front of the inner sanctuary; they were not seen outside; and they were there until this day.
verses.5:10: There was nothing in the ark except two tablets that Moses placed at Horeb, the things that the Lord covenanted with the sons of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt.
verses.5:11: And it happened, when the priests came out of the holy place, for all the priests who were found were consecrated; they were not arranged according to division.
verses.5:12: And all the Levites, the singers, belonging to the sons of Asaph, to Heman, to Jeduthun, and to his sons and his brothers, clothed in robes of fine linen, with cymbals and with harps and with lyres, were standing opposite the altar, and with them one hundred twenty priests blowing the trumpets.
verses.5:13: And there was one voice in blowing trumpets and in singing and in calling out with one voice to give thanks and to praise the Lord; and they lifted up their voice with trumpets and with cymbals and with instruments of songs, and they were saying, "Give thanks to the Lord, for it is good; for His mercy is forever." And the house was filled with a cloud of the glory of the Lord.
verses.5:14: And the priests were not able to stand to minister on account of the cloud, because the glory of the Lord filled the house of God.
verses.6:1: Then Solomon said, "The Lord said that He would dwell in thick darkness.
verses.6:2: And I have built a house for Your name, holy to You and prepared for You to dwell in forever."
verses.6:3: Then the king turned his face and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel was standing by.
verses.6:4: And he said, "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who spoke with His mouth to David my father and fulfilled it with His hands, saying,
verses.6:5: 'From the day that I brought My people up from the land of Egypt, I did not choose a city from all the tribes of Israel to build a house for My name to be there, and I did not choose a man to be leader over My people Israel;
verses.6:6: but I chose David to be over My people Israel.'
verses.6:7: And it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
verses.6:8: And the Lord said to David my father, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for My name, it was well in your heart;
verses.6:9: nevertheless, you will not build the house, for your son who will come out from your loins, he will build the house for My name.'
verses.6:10: And the Lord established this word that He spoke, and I came to be in place of David my father and sat on the throne of Israel just as the Lord spoke, and I built the house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel,
verses.6:11: and I placed the ark there, in which is the covenant of the Lord that He made with Israel."
verses.6:12: Then he stood in front of the altar of the Lord before the whole assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands;
verses.6:13: for Solomon had made a bronze platform and placed it in the middle of the courtyard of the sanctuary, five cubits was its length, five cubits its width, and three cubits its height; and he stood on it, and fell on his knees before the whole assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward heaven
verses.6:14: and said, "Lord, the God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven and on the earth, keeping the covenant and the mercy for Your servants who walk before You with a whole heart.
verses.6:15: You kept for Your servant David my father what You spoke in telling him, and You spoke with Your mouth and with Your hands fulfilled it, as it is this day.
verses.6:16: And now, Lord, the God of Israel, keep for Your servant David what You spoke to him, saying, 'A man will not fail you from the presence, sitting on the throne of Israel, if only your sons keep their way to walk in My name as you walked before Me.'
verses.6:17: And now, Lord, the God of Israel, let Your word indeed be confirmed that You spoke to Your servant David.
verses.6:18: For will God truly dwell with people on the earth? If heaven and the heaven of heaven will not suffice for You, then what is this house that I have built?
verses.6:19: Yet You will look upon the prayer of Your servant and upon my supplication, Lord God, to heed the supplication and the prayer before You today,
verses.6:20: that Your eyes may be open toward this house day and night, toward this place of which You said that Your name would be called upon there, to hear the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
verses.6:21: And You will hear the supplication of Your servant and of the people of Israel, whatever they pray toward this place; and You will listen in the place of Your dwelling from heaven, and You will hear and pardon.
verses.6:22: If a man sins against his neighbor and lays a curse on him to put him under a curse, and he comes and invokes the curse in front of the altar in this house,
verses.6:23: then You will listen from heaven and act, and judge Your servants, to repay the lawless one and return his ways upon his head, to vindicate the righteous one, to repay him according to his righteousness.
verses.6:24: And if Your people Israel are defeated in front of the enemy if they sin against You, and they turn back and confess to Your name and pray and make supplication before You in this house,
verses.6:25: then You will listen from heaven and pardon the sins of Your people Israel, and bring them back to the land that You gave to them and to their fathers.
verses.6:26: When heaven is shut up and there is no rain because they will sin against You, and they pray toward this place and praise Your name, and turn back from their sins because You will humble them;
verses.6:27: then You will listen from heaven and pardon the sins of Your servants and of Your people Israel, for You will show them the good way in which they will walk, and You will give rain upon Your land that You gave to Your people as an inheritance.
verses.6:28: If famine comes upon the land, if death comes upon the land, if blight and mildew, locust and caterpillar come, if the enemy oppresses them in front of their cities, concerning every plague and every distress,
verses.6:29: and every prayer and every supplication that may be made by any person and by all Your people Israel, if a person knows his affliction and his sickness, and spreads out his hands toward this house,
verses.6:30: then You will listen from heaven, from Your prepared dwelling place, and heal, and You will give to a man according to his ways, as You know his heart, for You alone know the heart of the sons of men;
verses.6:31: so that they may fear all Your ways all the days that they live on the face of the land that You gave to our fathers.
verses.6:32: And as for every foreigner who is not from the people of Israel, and comes from a distant land because of Your great name and Your mighty hand and Your uplifted arm, when they come and pray toward this place,
verses.6:33: then You will listen from heaven, from Your prepared dwelling place, and act according to everything for which the foreigner calls upon You, so that all the peoples of the earth may know Your name, and fear You like Your people Israel, and know that Your name has been called upon this house that I have built.
verses.6:34: Now if Your people go out to war against their enemies on the way by which You will send them, and they pray to You in the direction of this city that You chose, and of the house that I have built for Your name,
verses.6:35: then You will hear from heaven their supplication and their prayer, and execute their just cause.
verses.6:36: For they will sin against You (for there will be no person who will not sin), and You will strike them and hand them over before enemies, and those who capture them will take them captive to a land of enemies, to a land far or near,
verses.6:37: and should they turn their heart back in their land where they were led away, and indeed turn back and make supplication to You in their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted lawlessly,'
verses.6:38: and should they turn back to You with a whole heart and with all their soul in the land of those who took them captive, and pray in the direction of their land that You gave to their fathers, and of the city that You chose, and of the house that I built for Your name,
verses.6:39: then You will hear from heaven, from Your prepared dwelling place, their prayer and their supplication, and execute judgments, and pardon the people who sinned against You.
verses.6:40: Now, Lord, let Your eyes indeed be open and Your ears attentive to the supplication of this place.
verses.6:41: And now arise, Lord God, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength. May Your priests, Lord God, clothe themselves with salvation, and let Your sons rejoice in good things.
verses.6:42: Lord God, do not turn away Your face; remember the mercies of David Your servant."
verses.7:1: And when Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the whole burnt offerings and the sacrifices, and the glory of the Lord filled the house.
verses.7:2: And the priests were not able to enter the house of the Lord at that time, because the glory of the Lord filled the house.
verses.7:3: And all the sons of Israel were watching the fire coming down, and the glory of the Lord was upon the house; and they fell facedown to the ground on the stone pavement, and worshiped and were praising the Lord, "For it is good, for His mercy is forever."
verses.7:4: And the king and all the people were offering sacrifices before the Lord.
verses.7:5: And Solomon offered the sacrifice, twenty-two thousand calves, and the king dedicated the house of God; and all the people
verses.7:6: and the priests were standing at their posts, and the Levites with instruments of the songs of the Lord belonging to King David, to give thanks before the Lord, for His mercy is forever, with the hymns of David by their hand; and the priests were blowing the trumpets before them, and all Israel was standing.
verses.7:7: And Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard that was in the house of the Lord; for he offered there the whole burnt offerings and the fat portions of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that Solomon had made was not sufficient to receive the whole burnt offerings and the grain offerings and the fat portions.
verses.7:8: And Solomon held the festival at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of Egypt.
verses.7:9: And on the eighth day he held a closing assembly, for he held the dedication of the altar for seven days as a festival,
verses.7:10: and on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, rejoicing and with a glad heart for the good things that the Lord had done for David and for Solomon and for Israel His people.
verses.7:11: And Solomon finished the house of the Lord and the house of the king, and everything that Solomon formed in his soul to do in the house of the Lord and in his own house succeeded.
verses.7:12: And God appeared to Solomon by night and said to him, "I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for Myself as a house of sacrifice.
verses.7:13: If I shut up heaven and there is no rain, and if I command the locust to devour the trees, and if I send death among My people,
verses.7:14: and if My people, upon whom My name has been called, are humbled and pray and seek My face, and turn away from their evil ways, then I will listen from heaven and pardon their sins and heal their land.
verses.7:15: Now My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
verses.7:16: And now I have chosen and consecrated this house for My name to be there forever, and My eyes and My heart will be there all the days.
verses.7:17: And as for you, if you walk before Me like David your father, and act according to everything that I commanded you, and keep My statutes and My judgments,
verses.7:18: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom as I covenanted with David your father, saying, 'A man leading in Israel will not be removed from you.'
verses.7:19: But if you turn away, and forsake My statutes and My commandments that I set before you, and go and serve other gods and worship them,
verses.7:20: then I will remove you from the land that I gave to them, and this house that I consecrated for My name I will turn away from My presence, and I will make it a proverb and a tale among all the nations.
verses.7:21: And as for this lofty house, everyone who passes by it will be astonished and will say, 'For what reason has the Lord done this to this land and to this house?'
verses.7:22: And they will say, 'Because they forsook the Lord, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and worshiped them and served them; for this reason He brought all this calamity upon them.'"
verses.8:1: And it happened after twenty years, in which Solomon built the house of the Lord and his own house,
verses.8:2: that Solomon built the cities that Hiram had given to Solomon, and he settled the sons of Israel there.
verses.8:3: And Solomon went to Baisoba and overpowered it.
verses.8:4: And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and he built all the fortified cities in Hamath.
verses.8:5: And he built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, fortified cities with walls, gates, and bars,
verses.8:6: and Baalah, and all the fortified cities that belonged to Solomon, and all the cities of the chariots and the cities of the horsemen, and everything that Solomon desired according to his desire to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all his kingdom.
verses.8:7: All the people who were left from the Hittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Hivites and the Jebusites, who are not from Israel,
verses.8:8: were from their sons who were left with him in the land, whom the sons of Israel destroyed; and Solomon levied them for tribute until this day.
verses.8:9: And from the sons of Israel Solomon did not appoint any as servants for his kingdom, for look, they were fighting men and commanders, and the mighty men, and commanders of chariots and horsemen.
verses.8:10: And these were the commanders of the overseers of King Solomon, two hundred and fifty acting as taskmasters among the people.
verses.8:11: And Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh from the city of David to the house which he had built for her, for he said, "My wife will not live in the city of David, the king of Israel, because it is holy where the ark of the Lord entered."
verses.8:12: Then Solomon offered up burnt offerings to the Lord on the altar which he had built in front of the temple,
verses.8:13: and according to the requirement of each day, to offer up according to the commands of Moses on the Sabbaths and on the new moons and at the feasts, three times in the year: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, at the Feast of Weeks, at the Feast of Tabernacles.
verses.8:14: And he established according to the ordinance of David the divisions of the priests according to their ministries; and the Levites were at their posts to minister and to praise before the priests according to the requirement of each day; and the gatekeepers according to their divisions at each gate, for such were the commands of David, the man of God.
verses.8:15: They did not disregard the commands of the king concerning the priests and the Levites regarding any matter and regarding the treasuries.
verses.8:16: And all the work was made ready from the day it was founded until Solomon completed the house of the Lord.
verses.8:17: Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Elam by the sea in the land of Idumea.
verses.8:18: And Hiram sent by the hand of his servants ships and servants who knew the sea, and he went with the servants of Solomon to Sophira, and took from there the four hundred and fifty talents of gold, and they came to King Solomon.
verses.9:1: And the queen of Sheba heard of the name of Solomon, and came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with riddles, with a very great force and camels carrying spices and gold in abundance and precious stones; and she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was in her soul.
verses.9:2: And Solomon declared to her all her matters, and no matter escaped Solomon, a matter which he did not report to her.
verses.9:3: And the queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon, and the house which he had built,
verses.9:4: and the food of the tables, and the seating of his servants, and the standing of his ministers, and their clothing and that of his cupbearers, and their apparel, and the burnt offerings which he offered up in the house of the Lord; and she was beside herself.
verses.9:5: And she said to the king, "The word is true which I heard in my land concerning your words and concerning your wisdom.
verses.9:6: And I did not believe the words until I came and my eyes saw; and look, half of the abundance of your wisdom was not reported to me; you have surpassed the report that I heard.
verses.9:7: Blessed are the men, blessed are these servants of yours who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom.
verses.9:8: May the Lord your God be blessed, who took pleasure in you to set you on His throne as king for the Lord your God. Because the Lord your God loved Israel to establish it forever, He set you over them as king to execute justice and righteousness."
verses.9:9: And she gave to the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, and spices in great abundance, and precious stones; and there were none like those spices which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
verses.9:10: And the servants of Solomon and the servants of Hiram brought gold to Solomon from Suphir, and pine wood and precious stones.
verses.9:11: And the king made the pine wood into steps for the house of the Lord and for the house of the king, and lyres and harps for the singers; and such things had not been seen before in the land of Judah.
verses.9:12: And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desires which she asked for, besides all that she had brought to King Solomon; and she returned to her land.
verses.9:13: And the weight of the gold that was brought to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
verses.9:14: besides what the subordinate men and the merchants brought; and all the kings of Arabia and the satraps of the land brought gold and silver to King Solomon.
verses.9:15: And King Solomon made two hundred large shields of beaten gold; six hundred pure gold pieces were for each large shield, six hundred gold pieces were upon each large shield;
verses.9:16: and three hundred shields of beaten gold; and the king placed them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
verses.9:17: And the king made a great throne of ivory tusks, and overlaid it with refined gold.
verses.9:18: And there were six steps to the throne, bound with gold, and armrests on this side and on that side on the seating throne, and two lions standing beside the armrests.
verses.9:19: And twelve lions were standing there upon the six steps on this side and on that side; nothing like this was made in all the kingdom.
verses.9:20: And all the vessels of King Solomon were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were covered with gold; silver was not counted as anything in the days of Solomon.
verses.9:21: For a ship of the king went to Tarshish with the servants of Hiram; once every three years ships came from Tarshish to the king, full of gold and silver and ivory tusks and apes.
verses.9:22: And Solomon became greater than all the kings both in wealth and in wisdom.
verses.9:23: And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
verses.9:24: And they brought, each one his gifts: silver vessels and gold vessels and clothing, myrrh and sweet spices, horses and mules, year by year.
verses.9:25: And Solomon had four thousand mares for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he placed them in the cities of the chariots and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.9:26: And he was ruler over all the kings from the River even to the land of foreigners and to the borders of Egypt.
verses.9:27: And the king made the gold and the silver in Jerusalem like stones, and the cedars like the sycamore trees in the lowland in abundance.
verses.9:28: And the export of Solomon's horses was from Egypt and from all the earth.
verses.9:29: And the rest of the acts of Solomon, the first and the last, look, they are written in the words of Nathan the prophet and in the words of Ahijah the Shilonite and in the visions of Joel the seer concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.9:30: And King Solomon reigned over all Israel forty years.
verses.9:31: And Solomon slept, and they buried him in the city of David his father; and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:1: And Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel was coming to Shechem to make him king.
verses.10:2: And it happened when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it (and he was in Egypt, as he had fled from the presence of Solomon the king and Jeroboam lived in Egypt), that Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
verses.10:3: And he sent and called him; and Jeroboam came, and all the assembly came to Rehoboam, saying,
verses.10:4: "Your father made our yoke harsh; and now ease the harsh service of your father and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, and we will serve you."
verses.10:5: And he said to them, "Go for three days, and come to me." And the people departed.
verses.10:6: And King Rehoboam assembled the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he lived, saying, "How do you advise to give an answer to this people?"
verses.10:7: And they spoke to him, saying, "If today you are good to this people, and are favorably disposed and speak good words to them, then they will be servants to you all the days."
verses.10:8: And he abandoned the counsel of the elders who had counseled him, and took counsel with the young men who had been brought up with him, who stood before him.
verses.10:9: And he said to them, "What do you advise so that I may give an answer to this people who spoke to me, saying, 'Ease the yoke which your father put upon us'?"
verses.10:10: And the young men who had been brought up with him spoke to him, "Thus you will speak to the people who spoke to you, saying, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, and you, relieve us,' thus you will say, 'My little finger is thicker than the waist of my father.
verses.10:11: And now my father disciplined you with a heavy yoke, and I will add to our yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, and I will discipline you with scorpions.'"
verses.10:12: And Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had spoken, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
verses.10:13: And the king answered harshly, and King Rehoboam abandoned the counsel of the elders,
verses.10:14: and spoke to them according to the counsel of the younger men, saying, "My father made our yoke heavy, and I will add to it; my father disciplined you with whips, and I will discipline you with scorpions."
verses.10:15: And the king did not listen to the people, for there was a turn of events from God, saying, "The Lord established His word which He spoke by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat
verses.10:16: and all Israel, because the king did not listen to them." And the people answered the king, saying, "What portion is ours in David, and inheritance in the son of Jesse? To your tents, Israel! Now look to your house, David!" And all Israel went to its tents.
verses.10:17: And as for the men of Israel and those living in the cities of Judah, Jeroboam reigned over them.
verses.10:18: And Rehoboam sent Adoniram, who was over the tribute, to them, and the sons of Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. And King Jeroboam hurried to mount the chariot to flee to Jerusalem.
verses.10:19: And Israel broke faith with the house of David until this day.
verses.11:1: And Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, and he assembled Judah and Benjamin, one hundred eighty thousand young men making war; and he was fighting against Israel to return the kingdom to Rehoboam.
verses.11:2: And the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, a man of God, saying,
verses.11:3: "Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon and all Judah and Benjamin, saying,
verses.11:4: 'Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up and you shall not fight against your brothers. Turn back, each one to his house, because this matter has come about from Me.'" And they heeded the word of the Lord, and turned back from going against Jeroboam.
verses.11:5: And Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and he built walled cities in Judea.
verses.11:6: And he built Bethseem, Apan, and Tekoa,
verses.11:10: and Zorah, Aldon, and Hebron, which belongs to Judah and Benjamin, walled cities.
verses.11:11: And he fortified them as walled cities, and he placed commanders in them and stores of food, oil, and wine,
verses.11:12: in city after city, shields and spears, and he strengthened them to a very great degree. And Judah and Benjamin belonged to him.
verses.11:13: And the Levites and the priests who were in all Israel gathered to him from all the territories,
verses.11:14: for the Levites abandoned the dwellings of their possession and went to Judah, to Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons were driving them out from ministering to the Lord.
verses.11:15: And he appointed for himself priests of the high places, and for the idols, and for the worthless things, and for the calves that Jeroboam had made.
verses.11:16: And he drove them out from the tribes of Israel, those who gave their heart to seek the Lord, the God of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the Lord, the God of their fathers.
verses.11:17: And they strengthened the kingdom of Judah; and it strengthened Rehoboam the son of Solomon for three years, because he walked in the ways of David and Solomon for three years.
verses.11:18: And Rehoboam took for himself as a wife Mollath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, Baia the daughter of Elian the son of Jesse.
verses.11:19: And she bore him sons: Jauth, Shemariah, and Roollam.
verses.11:20: And after these things he took for himself Maacah the daughter of Absalom, and she bore him Abijah, Jeththi, Ziza, and Emmoth.
verses.11:21: And Rehoboam loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines, for he had eighteen wives and thirty concubines; and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
verses.11:22: And he appointed Abijah the son of Maacah as ruler, as leader among his brothers, because he intended to make him king.
verses.11:23: And he grew great beyond all his sons in all the territories of Judah and Benjamin and in the fortified cities, and he gave them provisions in great abundance, and he asked for a multitude of wives.
verses.12:1: And it came about, when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and when it was strengthened, that he abandoned the commands of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
verses.12:2: And it came about in the fifth year of the reign of Rehoboam that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had sinned before the Lord,
verses.12:3: with one thousand two hundred chariots and sixty thousand horses, and there was no number to the multitude that came with him out of Egypt: Libyans, Troglodytes, and Ethiopians.
verses.12:4: And they captured the fortified cities that were in Judah; and he came to Jerusalem.
verses.12:5: And Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and to the rulers of Judah who had gathered in Jerusalem from before Shishak, and said to them, "Thus said the Lord: 'You abandoned Me, and I will abandon you in the hand of Shishak.'"
verses.12:6: And the rulers of Israel and the king were ashamed, and they said, "The Lord is righteous."
verses.12:7: And when the Lord saw that they felt shame, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying, "They have felt shame; I will not destroy them, and I will give them, to a small extent, for deliverance, and My wrath will certainly not drip down in Jerusalem,
verses.12:8: for they will become servants, and they will know My service and the service of the kingdom of the earth."
verses.12:9: And Shishak king of Egypt came up, and he took the treasures that were in the house of the Lord and the treasures that were in the house of the king; he took everything; and he took the golden shields that Solomon had made.
verses.12:10: And Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place; and Shishak appointed over him captains of the runners, those guarding the gateway of the king.
verses.12:11: And it came about, whenever the king entered the house of the Lord, that the guards and the runners and those returning to meet the runners would go in.
verses.12:12: And when he felt shame, the anger of the Lord turned away from him, and not to complete destruction; for indeed in Judah there were good words.
verses.12:13: And Rehoboam grew strong in Jerusalem and reigned; and Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, in the city that the Lord chose to name His name there out of all the tribes of the sons of Israel; and the name of his mother was Naamah the Ammonite.
verses.12:14: And he did what was evil, because he did not direct his heart to seek out the Lord.
verses.12:15: And the acts of Rehoboam, the first and the last, see, are they not written in the words of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the seer, and his deeds? And Rehoboam fought against Jeroboam all the days.
verses.12:16: And Rehoboam died and was buried with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David; and Abijah his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:1: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Israel.
verses.13:2: He reigned three years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Maacah, the daughter of Uriel from Gibeon; and there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
verses.13:3: And Abijah drew up for battle with a force, warriors of valor, four hundred thousand mighty men; and Jeroboam drew up battle against him with eight hundred thousand, mighty warriors of valor.
verses.13:4: And Abijah rose up from Mount Somoron, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Listen, Jeroboam and all Israel!
verses.13:5: Is it not for you to know that the Lord, the God of Israel, gave a king over Israel forever to David and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
verses.13:6: And Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, rose up, and rose up away from his master.
verses.13:7: And pestilent men, lawless sons, gathered to him, and he rose up against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, and Rehoboam was rather young and timid in heart, and he did not withstand him to his face.
verses.13:8: And now you yourselves speak of withstanding the kingdom of the Lord through the hand of the sons of David; and you are a great multitude, and with you are golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.
verses.13:9: Or did you not drive out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and make for yourselves priests from the people of the whole land? Whoever came forward to fill his hands with calves from the cattle and with seven rams became a priest to that which is not God.
verses.13:10: And we have not abandoned the Lord our God, and His priests, the sons of Aaron, minister to the Lord, and the Levites in their divisions;
verses.13:11: they offer up in smoke to the Lord a burnt offering morning and evening, and compound incense, and arrangements of bread on the pure table, and the golden lampstand and the lamps for burning to light in the evening; for we ourselves keep the charges of the Lord, the God of our fathers, and you have abandoned Him.
verses.13:12: And look, with us at the head is the Lord, and His priests, and the signal trumpets to sound the signal over us. Sons of Israel, you will fight against the Lord, the God of our fathers, for it will not go well for you."
verses.13:13: And Jeroboam sent the ambush around to come behind them; and he was in front of Judah, and the ambush was behind.
verses.13:14: And Judah turned around, and look, the battle was against them from the front and from behind; and they cried out to the Lord, and the priests sounded the trumpets.
verses.13:15: And the men of Judah cried out; and it came about, as the men of Judah cried out, that the Lord struck Jeroboam and Israel before Abijah and Judah.
verses.13:16: And the sons of Israel fled from before Judah, and the Lord delivered them into their hands.
verses.13:17: And Abijah and his people struck a great blow among them, and five hundred thousand mighty men from Israel fell wounded.
verses.13:18: And the sons of Israel were humbled on that day, and the sons of Judah grew strong, because they hoped in the Lord, the God of their fathers.
verses.13:19: And Abijah pursued after Jeroboam and captured cities from him: Bethel and its villages, and Cana and its villages, and Ephron and its villages.
verses.13:20: And Jeroboam no longer had strength all the days of Abijah, and the Lord struck him, and he died.
verses.13:21: And Abijah grew strong, and he took for himself fourteen wives, and he fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
verses.13:22: And the rest of the acts of Abijah, and his deeds, and his words, are written in the book of the prophet Iddo.
verses.13:23: And Abijah died with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Asa his son reigned in his place. In the days of Asa, the land of Judah was at rest for ten years.
verses.14:1: And he did what was good and right before the Lord his God.
verses.14:2: And he removed the altars of the foreigners and the high places, and he shattered the pillars and cut down the groves.
verses.14:3: And he told Judah to seek out the Lord God of their fathers and to do the law and the commandments.
verses.14:4: And he removed from all the cities of Judah the altars and the idols, and he was at peace.
verses.14:5: Fortified cities were in the land of Judah, because the land was at peace; and he had no war in those years, because the Lord gave him rest.
verses.14:6: And he said to Judah, "Let us build these cities, and let us make walls and towers and gates and bars; we will have dominion before the land, because just as we sought the Lord our God, He sought us out, and gave us rest all around and granted us success."
verses.14:7: And Asa had an army of armed men carrying large shields and spears in the land of Judah, three hundred thousand, and in the land of Benjamin, light-shield bearers and archers, two hundred and fifty thousand; all these were mighty warriors.
verses.14:8: And Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army, with thousands and three hundred chariots, and he came as far as Marisel.
verses.14:9: And Asa went out to meet him, and drew up battle lines in the valley to the north of Mareshah.
verses.14:10: And Asa cried out to the Lord his God and said, "Lord, it is not impossible with You to save with many and with few; strengthen us, Lord our God, because we have trusted in You, and in Your name we have come against this great multitude. Lord our God, do not let man prevail against You."
verses.14:11: And the Lord struck the Ethiopians before Judah, and the Ethiopians fled.
verses.14:12: And Asa and his people pursued them as far as Gedor; and the Ethiopians fell so that there was no survival among them, because they were shattered before the Lord and before His army; and they plundered much spoil.
verses.14:13: And they destroyed their villages around Gedor, because terror of the Lord came upon them; and they plundered all its cities, because much spoil belonged to them.
verses.14:14: And they also destroyed the tents of possessions, the Amazoneis, and they took many sheep and camels, and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.15:1: And as for Azariah son of Oded, the Spirit of the Lord came upon him.
verses.15:2: And he went out to meet them in all Judah and Benjamin, and said, "The Lord is with you while we are with Him; and if you seek Him out, He will be found by you; and if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.
verses.15:3: And there are many days for Israel without a true God and without law.
verses.15:4: And He will turn them back to the Lord God of Israel, and He will be found by them.
verses.15:5: And in that time there is no peace for the one coming in and for the one going out, because terror of the Lord is upon all who inhabit the lands.
verses.15:6: And nation will fight against nation and city against city, because God terrified them in every distress.
verses.15:7: And you, be strong, and do not let your hands grow weak, because there is a reward for your work."
verses.15:8: And when he heard these words and the prophecy of Adad the prophet, he grew strong and cast out the abominations from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities that he had seized in Mount Ephraim, and he renewed the altar of the Lord that was in front of the temple of the Lord.
verses.15:9: And he assembled Judah and Benjamin and the proselytes who were residing with him from Ephraim and from Manasseh and from Simeon, because many of Israel joined themselves to him when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.
verses.15:10: And they were gathered to Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
verses.15:11: And he sacrificed to the Lord on that day from what he had brought: seven hundred calves and seven thousand sheep.
verses.15:12: And he entered into a covenant to seek the Lord God of their fathers with the whole heart and with the whole soul.
verses.15:13: And everyone who does not seek out the Lord God of Israel will die, from young to old, from man to woman.
verses.15:14: And they swore by the Lord with a loud voice and with trumpets.
verses.15:15: And all Judah rejoiced over the oath, because they swore with all their soul and sought Him with full desire, and He was found by them, and the Lord gave them rest all around.
verses.15:16: And he removed his mother Maacah from ministering to Astarte, and he cut the idol to pieces and burned it in the brook Kidron.
verses.15:17: Yet the high places were not removed; they still existed in Israel; but the heart of Asa was whole all his days.
verses.15:18: And he brought in the holy things of David his father and the holy things of the house of the Lord God: silver and gold and vessels.
verses.15:19: And there was no war with him until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.
verses.16:1: And in the thirty-eighth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah so as not to allow exit and entrance to Asa king of Judah.
verses.16:2: And Asa took gold and silver from the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the house of the king, and sent to the son of Hader, king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying,
verses.16:3: "Make a covenant between me and you, and between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you gold and silver; come and scatter Baasha king of Israel away from me, and let him depart from me."
verses.16:4: And the son of Hader listened to King Asa, and sent to the commanders of his army against the cities of Israel, and he struck Io and Dano and Abelman and all the surrounding districts of Naphtali.
verses.16:5: And it happened, when Baasha heard, that he stopped building Ramah any longer and ceased his work.
verses.16:6: And King Asa took all Judah, and he took the stones of Ramah and its timbers with which Baasha had built, and with them he built Geba and Mizpah.
verses.16:7: And at that time Hanami the prophet came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you trusted in the king of Syria and did not trust in the Lord your God, therefore the army of Syria escaped from your hand.
verses.16:8: Were not the Ethiopians and Libyans a great army, with boldness, with horsemen in a very great multitude? And when you trusted in the Lord, He delivered them into your hands.
verses.16:9: For the eyes of the Lord look throughout all the earth to show strength in every heart that is whole concerning what is toward Him. You have acted ignorantly in this; from now on there is war with you."
verses.16:10: And Asa became angry with the prophet, and put him in prison because of this; and Asa did harm among the people at that time.
verses.16:11: And look, the acts of Asa, the first and the last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.16:12: And Asa became ill in his feet in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, until he became exceedingly ill; and in his illness he did not seek the Lord, but the physicians.
verses.16:13: And Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the thirtieth year of his reign.
verses.16:14: And they buried him in the tomb that he had dug for himself in the city of David, and they laid him on the bier and filled it with spices and kinds of perfumers' ointments, and they made a very great funeral for him.
verses.17:1: And Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place, and Jehoshaphat grew strong against Israel.
verses.17:2: And he placed a force in all the fortified cities of Judah, and appointed leaders in all the cities of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had previously captured.
verses.17:3: And the Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father, and he did not seek the idols,
verses.17:4: but he sought the Lord, the God of his father, and walked in the commandments of his father, and not like the deeds of Israel.
verses.17:5: And the Lord established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah gave gifts to Jehoshaphat, and he had wealth and much glory.
verses.17:6: And his heart was lifted up in the way of the Lord, and he removed the high places and the groves from the land of Judah.
verses.17:7: And in the third year of his reign he sent his leaders and the sons of the mighty men, Abijah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah.
verses.17:8: And with them were the Levites: Samuas, Manthanias, Zebadiah, Jasiel, Shemiramoth, Jonathan, Adonijah, and Tobadobiah, Levites; those with them were Elishama and Joram, the priests.
verses.17:9: And they taught in Judah, and with them was the book of the law of the Lord; and they went through the cities of Judah and taught the people.
verses.17:10: And a dread of the Lord came upon all the kingdoms of the land around Judah, and they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.
verses.17:11: And some of the foreigners brought gifts and silver and presents to Jehoshaphat, and the Arabs brought him seven thousand seven hundred rams of sheep.
verses.17:12: And Jehoshaphat kept growing greater, even to great height, and he built dwellings in Judea and fortified cities.
verses.17:13: And there were many works in Judea, and men of war, mighty and strong, were in Jerusalem.
verses.17:14: And this is their number according to their fathers' houses; and for Judah, commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand sons mighty in strength;
verses.17:15: and after him Johanan the leader, and with him two hundred eighty thousand;
verses.17:16: and after him Masaias son of Zari, who volunteered for the Lord, and with him two hundred thousand mighty in strength.
verses.17:17: And from Benjamin, a mighty man of strength, even Eliada, and with him two hundred thousand archers and shield-bearers;
verses.17:18: and after him Jehozabad, and with him one hundred eighty thousand mighty in war.
verses.17:19: These were those who served the king, besides those whom the king placed in the fortified cities in all Judea.
verses.18:1: And Jehoshaphat still had wealth and much glory, and he allied himself by marriage with the house of Ahab.
verses.18:2: And at the end of some years he went down to Ahab in Samaria, and Ahab slaughtered many sheep and calves for him and for the people who were with him, and he coaxed him to go up with him to Ramoth of Gilead.
verses.18:3: And Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth of Gilead?" And he said to him, "As I am, so also are you; as my people, so also your people, with you in war."
verses.18:4: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please inquire of the Lord today."
verses.18:5: And the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall I go to Ramoth-gilead to war, or shall I refrain?" And they said, "Go up, and God will give it into the hands of the king."
verses.18:6: And Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not still a prophet of the Lord here, that we may inquire from him?"
verses.18:7: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom to inquire of the Lord, and I have hated him, because he does not prophesy concerning me for good, for all his days are for evil; this is Micaiah son of Jemaa." And Jehoshaphat said, "Do not let the king speak like this."
verses.18:8: And the king called one eunuch and said, "Quickly, Micaiah son of Jemaa!"
verses.18:9: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each on his throne and clothed in robes, sitting in the open square at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
verses.18:10: And Zedekiah son of Canaan made for himself horns of iron and said, "Thus says the Lord: 'With these you will gore Syria until it is consumed.'"
verses.18:11: And all the prophets were prophesying like this, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and you will prosper, and the Lord will give it into the hands of the king."
verses.18:12: And the messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, "Look, the prophets have spoken good things concerning the king with one mouth; so please let your words be like those of one of them, and you will speak good things."
verses.18:13: And Micaiah said, "As the Lord lives, whatever God says to me, that I will speak."
verses.18:14: And he came to the king, and the king said to him, "Micaiah, shall I go to Ramoth-gilead to war, or shall I refrain?" And he said, "Go up, and you will prosper, and they will be given into your hands."
verses.18:15: And the king said to him, "How many times do I put you under oath not to speak to me anything except the truth in the name of the Lord?"
verses.18:16: And he said, "I saw Israel scattered in the mountains like sheep that have no shepherd; and the Lord said, 'They do not have a leader; let each one return to his house in peace.'"
verses.18:17: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not say to you that he does not prophesy good concerning me, but only evil?"
verses.18:18: And he said, "Not so! Hear the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven was standing on His right and on His left.
verses.18:19: And the Lord said, 'Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, so that he will go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' And one said this, and another said that.
verses.18:20: And the spirit came forward and stood before the Lord and said, 'I will deceive him.' And the Lord said, 'By what means?'
verses.18:21: And it said, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And He said, 'You will deceive him, you will prevail; go out and do so.'
verses.18:22: And now, look, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken evil against you."
verses.18:23: And Zedekiah son of Canaan came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said to him, "By what way—a spirit from me, a spirit to you, the Spirit of the Lord from me to speak to you?"
verses.18:24: And Micaiah said, "Look, you will see on that day; he will enter an inner room from an inner room to hide himself."
verses.18:25: And the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and return him to Emer, ruler of the city, and to Joash the ruler, son of the king,
verses.18:26: and say, 'Thus said the king: Put this man in the prison house, and let him eat bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace.'"
verses.18:27: And Micaiah said, "If you indeed return in peace, the Lord has not spoken by me. Hear, all peoples!"
verses.18:28: And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.18:29: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Disguise me, and I will enter into the battle; and you, put on my clothing." And the king of Israel disguised himself and entered into the battle.
verses.18:30: And the king of Syria commanded the commanders of the chariots who were with him, saying, "Do not fight the small or the great, but only the king of Israel."
verses.18:31: And it happened, when the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, "He is the king of Israel," and they surrounded him to fight. And Jehoshaphat cried out, and the Lord saved him, and God turned them away from him.
verses.18:32: And it happened, when the commanders of the chariots saw that he was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from him.
verses.18:33: And a man drew a bow with sure aim and struck the king of Israel between the lung and the breastplate; and he said to the charioteer, "Turn your hand around and bring me out of the battle, for I am wounded."
verses.18:34: And the battle turned on that day, and the king of Israel was standing in the chariot until evening facing Syria, and he died as the sun was setting.
verses.19:1: And Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned to his house in Jerusalem.
verses.19:2: And Jehu son of Hanani the prophet went out to meet him and said to him, "King Jehoshaphat, do you help a sinner, or make friends with one hated by the Lord? Because of this, wrath has come upon you from the Lord;
verses.19:3: yet good things have been found in you, because you removed the groves from the land of Judah and directed your heart to seek the Lord."
verses.19:4: And Jehoshaphat stayed, and again went out to the people from Beersheba to Mount Ephraim, and turned them back to the Lord, the God of their fathers.
verses.19:5: And he appointed judges in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city.
verses.19:6: And he said to the judges, "See what you are doing, for you do not judge for man, but for the Lord, and with you are the matters of judgment.
verses.19:7: And now, let the fear of the Lord be upon you; be careful and act, for there is no injustice with the Lord our God, nor showing partiality, nor taking gifts."
verses.19:8: And indeed in Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appointed some of the priests and of the Levites and of the patriarchs of Israel for the judgment of the Lord and to judge those who dwell in Jerusalem.
verses.19:9: And he commanded them, saying, "In this way you are to act in the fear of the Lord, in truth and with a full heart:
verses.19:10: As for every man, the case that comes before you of our brothers who dwell in the midst of blood, and between ordinance and commandment, and statutes and judgments; you will warn them, and they will not sin against the Lord, and wrath will not be upon you and upon your brothers. In this way you are to act, and you will not sin.
verses.19:11: And look, Amariah the priest is leader over you for every matter of the Lord, and Zebadiah is the leader over the house of Judah for every matter of the king, and the scribes and the Levites are before you. Be strong and act, and the Lord will be with the good."
verses.20:1: And after these things, the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and with them some of the Meunites, came against Jehoshaphat for war.
verses.20:2: And some came and reported to Jehoshaphat, saying, "A great multitude has come against you from beyond the sea, from Syria; and look, they are in Hasam Thamara, which is En-gedi."
verses.20:3: And he was afraid, and Jehoshaphat set his face to seek the Lord, and they proclaimed a fast.
verses.20:4: And Judah gathered together to seek the Lord, and from all the cities Judah came to seek the Lord.
verses.20:5: And Jehoshaphat stood up in the assembly of Judah in Jerusalem, in the house of the Lord, before the new court,
verses.20:6: and said, "Lord God of our fathers, are You not God in heaven above? And You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations, and in Your hand is strength of might, and there is no standing against You.
verses.20:7: Did You not, Lord, utterly destroy the inhabitants of this land from before Israel and give it to the seed of Abraham, Your beloved, forever?
verses.20:8: And they lived in it, and built in it a sanctuary for Your name, saying,
verses.20:9: 'If evils come upon us, sword, judgment, death, famine, we will stand before the house and before You, for Your name is upon this house, and we will cry out to You from the distress, and You will hear and save.'
verses.20:10: And now, look, the sons of Ammon and Mount Seir, through whom You did not allow Israel to pass when they came out of the land of Egypt, for they turned aside from them and did not utterly destroy them;
verses.20:11: and now, look, they are attacking us, coming out to drive us out from our inheritance that You gave us,
verses.20:12: Lord our God, will You not pass judgment on them? For we have no strength to stand against this great multitude that has come against us, and we do not know what we should do to them, but our eyes are upon You."
verses.20:13: And all Judah was standing before the Lord, along with their little children and wives.
verses.20:14: And as for Oziel, the son of Zechariah, of the sons of Eleael, the son of Manthanias, the Levite from the sons of Asaph, the Spirit of the Lord came upon him in the assembly,
verses.20:15: and he said, "Listen, all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem and King Jehoshaphat! Thus says the Lord to you yourselves: 'Do not be afraid nor be terrified before this great crowd, for the battle is not yours, but God's.
verses.20:16: Tomorrow go down against them; look, they are going up by the ascent of Hasae, and you will find them at the end of the river of the wilderness of Jeriel.
verses.20:17: It is not for you to fight; understand these things and see the salvation of the Lord with you! Look, also Jerusalem: do not be terrified nor be afraid of him to go out to meet them, and the Lord is with you.'"
verses.20:18: And Jehoshaphat bowed down upon his face, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell before the Lord to worship the Lord.
verses.20:19: And the Levites from the sons of Kohath and from the sons of Korah stood up to praise the Lord God of Israel with a loud voice on high.
verses.20:20: And they rose early in the morning and went out into the wilderness of Tekoa; and as they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and cried out, "Listen to me, Judah and those living in Jerusalem! Trust in the Lord your God, and you will be trusted; trust in His prophet, and you will prosper."
verses.20:21: And he took counsel with the people, and appointed psalm-singers and praisers to give thanks and to praise the holy things as they went out before the army; and he was saying, "Give thanks to the Lord, for His mercy is forever."
verses.20:22: And when he began his praise of thanksgiving, the Lord caused the sons of Ammon to fight against Moab and Mount Seir, who had come out against Judah, and they were routed.
verses.20:23: And the sons of Ammon and Moab revolted against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to utterly destroy and wipe them out; and when they had finished off the inhabitants of Seir, they rose up against one another to be utterly destroyed.
verses.20:24: And Judah came to the lookout of the wilderness, and looked out and saw the multitude; and look, all were dead, fallen upon the ground; there was no one who escaped.
verses.20:25: And Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their spoil, and they found much livestock and possessions and spoil and desirable vessels, and he plundered among them; and there were three days of their plundering the spoil, for it was plentiful.
verses.20:26: And it came about on the fourth day that they assembled together in the valley of blessing, for there they blessed the Lord; therefore they called the name of that place Valley of Blessing until this day.
verses.20:27: And every man of Judah returned to Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat leading them, in great gladness, because the Lord made them glad over their enemies.
verses.20:28: And they entered into Jerusalem with harps and with lyres and with trumpets, into the house of the Lord.
verses.20:29: And dread of the Lord came upon all the kingdoms of the earth when they heard that the Lord had fought against the adversaries of Israel.
verses.20:30: And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at peace, and his God gave him rest on every side.
verses.20:31: And Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah; he was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Azubah, daughter of Shilhi.
verses.20:32: And he walked in the ways of his father Asa, and did not turn aside from doing what was right before the Lord.
verses.20:33: However, the high places still remained, and still the people had not directed their heart to the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.20:34: And the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, the first and the last, look, they are written in the words of Joshua the son of Hanani, who wrote the book of the king of Israel.
verses.20:35: And after these things Jehoshaphat partnered with Ahaziah king of Israel, and he committed lawlessness
verses.20:36: in acting and going to him to make ships to go to Tarshish; and he made ships in Ezion-geber.
verses.20:37: And Eliada the son of Odeia from Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you befriended Ahaziah, the Lord has shattered your work, and your ships have been wrecked." And he was not able to go to Tarshish.
verses.21:1: And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David; and his son Joram reigned in his place.
verses.21:2: And he had six brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat: Jehiel, Zechariah, Mishael, and Shephatiah; all these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
verses.21:3: And their father gave them many gifts, silver and gold and weapons, along with fortified cities in Judah; but the kingdom he gave to Joram, because he was the firstborn.
verses.21:4: And Joram rose up over his kingdom and grew strong, and killed all his brothers with the sword, and some of the officials of Israel.
verses.21:5: When he was thirty-two years old, Joram was established over his kingdom, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.21:6: And he walked in the way of the king of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for a daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did what was evil before the Lord.
verses.21:7: Yet the Lord was not willing to utterly destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that He had made with David, and as He had said to him, to give a lamp to him and to his sons all the days.
verses.21:8: In those days Edom revolted from Judah, and they installed a king over themselves.
verses.21:9: And Joram went out with the commanders, and all the cavalry with him; and it came about that he arose by night and struck Edom, who was surrounding him, and the commanders of the chariots; and the people fled to their tents.
verses.21:10: And Edom revolted from Judah until this day; then Libnah revolted at that time from his hand, because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers.
verses.21:11: Moreover, he himself made high places in the cities of Judah, and they led those living in Jerusalem into prostitution, and he led Judah astray.
verses.21:12: And it came to him in writing from Elijah the prophet, saying, "Thus says the Lord, God of your father David: 'Because you have not walked in the way of Jehoshaphat your father and in the ways of Asa king of Judah,
verses.21:13: and have walked in the ways of the king of Israel, and have led Judah and those living in Jerusalem into prostitution, as the house of Ahab committed prostitution, and have killed your brothers, the sons of your father, who were better than you;
verses.21:14: look, the Lord will strike you with a great blow in your people and in your sons and in your wives and in all your possessions;
verses.21:15: and you yourself will be in a severe sickness, in a disease of the bowels, until your bowels come out with the sickness day after day.'"
verses.21:16: And the Lord stirred up against Joram the foreigners and the Arabs and those bordering the Ethiopians;
verses.21:17: and they went up against Judah and overpowered it, and carried off all the possessions that they found in the house of the king, and his sons and his daughters, and no son was left to him except Ahaziah, the youngest of his sons.
verses.21:18: And after all these things, the Lord struck him in the bowels with a sickness for which there is no cure.
verses.21:19: And it went on day after day; and when the time of the days came, two days, his bowels came out with the disease, and he died in a severe sickness; and his people did not make a funeral like the funeral of his fathers.
verses.21:20: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem; and he departed without praise, and was buried in the city of David, and not in the tombs of the kings.
verses.22:1: And those living in Jerusalem made Ahaziah, his youngest son, king in his place, for the raiding band that had come upon them, the Arabs, the Alimazonites, had killed all the older ones; and Ahaziah son of Joram king of Judah became king.
verses.22:2: Ahaziah was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri.
verses.22:3: He also walked in the way of the house of Ahab, for his mother was a counselor to sin.
verses.22:4: And he did what was evil before the Lord like the house of Ahab, for they were counselors to him after his father died, to utterly destroy him,
verses.22:5: and he walked in their counsels. And he went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria to Ramoth-gilead; and the archers struck Joram.
verses.22:6: And Joram returned to Israel to be healed from the wounds with which the Syrians had struck him in Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Syria; and Ahaziah son of Joram, king of Judah, went down to Israel to see Joram son of Ahab, because he was sick.
verses.22:7: And the downfall of Ahaziah came from God in coming to Joram; and when he went out, Joram went out with him to the son of Nimshi, the anointed of the Lord, the house of Ahab.
verses.22:8: And it came about when Jehu took vengeance on the house of Ahab, that they found the officials of Judah and the brothers of Ahaziah serving Ahaziah, and he killed them.
verses.22:9: And he commanded to seek Ahaziah; and they captured him while he was being healed in Samaria and brought him to Jehu, and he killed him. And they buried him, for they said, "He is a son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart." And there was no one in the house of Ahaziah to hold power concerning the kingdom.
verses.22:10: And Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, and she arose and destroyed all the seed of the kingdom in the house of Judah.
verses.22:11: And Jehosheba took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him from the midst of the king's sons who were being put to death, and put him and his nurse into a chamber of beds; and Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah and wife of Jehoiada, hid him; and she hid him from before Athaliah, and she did not kill him.
verses.22:12: And he was hidden with him in the house of God for six years, and Athaliah reigned over the land.
verses.23:1: And in the eighth year Jehoiada grew strong and took the commanders of hundreds, Azariah son of Joram and Ishmael son of Jehohanan and Azariah son of Obed and Maaseiah son of Aziah and Elishaphan son of Zechariah, with him into a house.
verses.23:2: And they went around Judah, and he gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah and the leaders of the families of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
verses.23:3: And the entire assembly of Judah made a covenant in the house of God with the king; and he showed them the king's son and said to them, "Look, let the king's son reign, just as the Lord spoke concerning the house of David.
verses.23:4: Now this is the thing that you shall do: let a third of you, of the priests and of the Levites, come in on the Sabbath, and at the gates of the entrances,
verses.23:5: and a third in the house of the king, and a third at the middle gate, and all the people in the courts of the house of the Lord.
verses.23:6: And let no one enter into the house of the Lord except the priests and the Levites and those of the Levites who minister; they shall enter, because they are holy; and let all the people keep the watches for the Lord.
verses.23:7: And the Levites shall surround the king all around, each man with his every weapon in his hand, and the one who enters into the house shall die; and they shall be with the king as he comes in and goes out."
verses.23:8: And the Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded; and each one took his men from the beginning of the Sabbath until the close of the Sabbath, because Jehoiada did not dismiss the divisions.
verses.23:9: And he gave the swords and the shields and the weapons that belonged to King David in the house of God.
verses.23:10: And he stationed all the people, each one with his weapons, from the right side of the house to the left side of the altar and of the house, all around the king.
verses.23:11: And he brought out the king's son, and placed upon him the crown and the testimonies; and Jehoiada and his sons made him king and anointed him, and said, "May the king live!"
verses.23:12: And Athaliah heard the sound of the people running and giving thanks and praising the king, and she came to the king into the house of the Lord.
