verses.23:13: And she looked, and see, the king was at his station, and at the entrance were the leaders and the trumpets, leaders around the king, and all the people rejoiced and blew the trumpets, and those singing with the instruments, singers and those chanting praise; and Athaliah tore her robe and cried out, "You are surely conspiring!"
verses.23:14: And Jehoiada the priest went out; and Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds and the chiefs of the army and said to them, "Drive her outside the house, and go in after her, and let her die by the sword." For the priest said, "Let her not die in the house of the Lord."
verses.23:15: And they gave her room, and she passed through the gate of the horsemen of the house of the king, and they put her to death there.
verses.23:16: And Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and the people and the king, to be a people for the Lord.
verses.23:17: And all the people of the land entered into the house of Baal, and tore it down, and its altars and its idols, and crushed them fine; and they put Mattan the priest of Baal to death before his altars.
verses.23:18: And Jehoiada the priest undertook the works of the house of the Lord by the hand of priests and Levites, and he set up the divisions of the priests and of the Levites, which David had assigned over the house of the Lord, and to offer up burnt offerings to the Lord, just as it is written in the law of Moses, with gladness and with songs by the hand of David.
verses.23:19: And the gatekeepers stood at the gates of the house of the Lord, and no one unclean in any matter shall enter.
verses.23:20: And he took the patriarchs and the mighty men and the leaders of the people and all the people of the land, and they brought the king up into the house of the Lord, and he entered through the inner gate into the house of the king, and they seated the king upon the throne of the kingdom.
verses.23:21: And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city became quiet; and they put Athaliah to death.
verses.24:1: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Abiah from Beersheba.
verses.24:2: And Joash did what was right in the sight of the Lord all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
verses.24:3: And Jehoiada took for himself two wives, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.24:4: And it came about after these things that it came upon the heart of Joash to repair the house of the Lord.
verses.24:5: And he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah and collect from all Israel money to strengthen the house of the Lord year by year, and hasten to speak." And the Levites did not believe.
verses.24:6: And King Joash called Jehoiada the leader and said to him, "Why have you not inquired concerning the Levites, to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem what was decreed by Moses the man of God, because he assembled Israel to the tent of the testimony?"
verses.24:7: For Athaliah was the lawless one, and her sons tore down the house of God, and indeed they used the sacred things of the house of the Lord for the Baals.
verses.24:8: And the king said, "Let a chest be made and let it be placed at the gate of the house of the Lord outside.
verses.24:9: And let them proclaim in Judah and in Jerusalem to bring in to the Lord, just as Moses the servant of God spoke concerning Israel in the wilderness."
verses.24:10: And all the leaders and all the people gave, and they kept bringing it in and dropping it into the chest until it was filled.
verses.24:11: And it came about, when they brought the chest in to the officers of the king by the hand of the Levites, and when they saw that the money was abundant, that the scribe of the king and the officer of the high priest came and emptied the chest, and set it back in its place; thus they did day by day, and they collected much money.
verses.24:12: And the king and Jehoiada the priest gave it to those doing the works for the work of the house of the Lord; and they hired stonecutters and carpenters to repair the house of the Lord, and smiths of iron and bronze to repair the house of the Lord.
verses.24:13: And those doing the works kept working, and the extent of the works went up in their hands, and they restored the house of the Lord to its standing and strengthened it.
verses.24:14: And when they had finished, they brought to the king and to Jehoiada the remainder of the money, and they made utensils for the house of the Lord, service utensils for burnt offerings and censers of gold and silver; and they offered up burnt offerings in the house of the Lord continually all the days of Jehoiada.
verses.24:15: And Jehoiada grew old, full of days, and he died, being one hundred and thirty years old when he died.
verses.24:16: And they buried him in the city of David with the kings, because he had done good with Israel and with God and His house.
verses.24:17: And it came about after the death of Jehoiada that the leaders of Judah came in and bowed down to the king; then the king listened to them.
verses.24:18: And they forsook the Lord, the God of their fathers, and served the Astartes and the idols; and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem on that day.
verses.24:19: And He sent prophets to them to turn them back to the Lord, and they did not listen; and they testified against them, and they did not obey.
verses.24:20: And the Spirit of God clothed Azariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood up above the people and said, "Thus says the Lord, 'Why do you transgress the commandments of the Lord? And you will not prosper; because you have forsaken the Lord, He also will forsake you.'"
verses.24:21: And they conspired against him, and stoned him by the command of King Joash in the court of the house of the Lord.
verses.24:22: And Joash did not remember the mercy that Jehoiada his father had shown him, and he put his son to death. And as he was dying, he said, "May the Lord see and judge!"
verses.24:23: And it came about after the completion of the year that the army of Syria went up against him, and came against Judah and against Jerusalem; and they destroyed all the leaders of the people among the people, and sent all their plunder to the king of Damascus.
verses.24:24: For the army of Syria arrived with few men, and God delivered into their hands a very great army, because they had forsaken the Lord, the God of their fathers; and He executed judgments on Joash.
verses.24:25: And after they departed from him, when they left him in severe illnesses, his servants conspired against him because of the bloodshed of the son of Jehoiada the priest, and they put him to death on his bed, and he died; and they buried him in the city of David, but they did not bury him in the tomb of the kings.
verses.24:26: And those who conspired against him were Zabel the son of Sama the Ammonite and Zozabed the son of Somaioth the Moabite,
verses.24:27: and all his sons, and the five came to him. And the rest, look, are written in the record of the kings; and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.25:1: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Jonaa from Jerusalem.
verses.25:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord, yet not with a full heart.
verses.25:3: And it came about, when the kingdom was established in his hand, that he put to death his servants who had murdered the king his father.
verses.25:4: Yet he did not kill their sons, according to the covenant of the law of the Lord, just as it is written, as the Lord commanded, saying, "Fathers shall not die for children, and sons shall not die for fathers; rather, each shall die for his own sin."
verses.25:5: And Amaziah assembled the house of Judah, and stationed them according to their fathers' houses under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds for all Judah and Jerusalem; and he numbered them from twenty years old and upward, and found them to be three hundred thousand, able to go out to war, holding spear and shield.
verses.25:6: And he hired from Israel one hundred thousand, mighty in strength, for one hundred talents of silver.
verses.25:7: And a man of God came to him, saying, "King, the army of Israel shall not go with you, because the Lord is not with Israel, all the sons of Ephraim.
verses.25:8: For if you think you will prevail with these, then the Lord will rout you before the enemies, because it belongs to the Lord both to give strength and to rout."
verses.25:9: And Amaziah said to the man of God, "And what shall I do about the one hundred talents that I gave to the army of Israel?" And the man of God said, "The Lord is able to give you far more than these."
verses.25:10: And Amaziah separated the army that had come to him from Ephraim, to depart to their own place; and they became very angry against Judah, and returned to their own place in furious anger.
verses.25:11: And Amaziah grew strong and took his people, and went to the Valley of Salt, and struck down ten thousand of the sons of Seir there.
verses.25:12: And the sons of Judah captured ten thousand alive, and brought them to the top of the cliff, and hurled them down from the top of the cliff, and all of them were broken to pieces.
verses.25:13: And the sons of the army whom Amaziah had sent back so as not to be found with him for war attacked the cities of Judah from Samaria to Beth-horon, and struck down three thousand among them, and plundered much spoil.
verses.25:14: And it came about, after Amaziah arrived from striking down Idumea, that he brought to them the gods of the sons of Seir, and set them up for himself as gods, and stood before them to bow down, and he himself was sacrificing to them.
verses.25:15: And the wrath of the Lord came upon Amaziah, and He sent prophets to him, and they said to him, "Why did you seek the gods of the people who did not rescue their own people from your hand?"
verses.25:16: And it came about as he spoke to him, that he said to him, "Have I made you counselor of the king? Take care that you are not flogged." And the prophet became silent, and said, "I know that He purposed against you to destroy you, because you did this and did not listen to my counsel."
verses.25:18: And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The chozei in Lebanon sent to the cedar that is in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife,' and look, the wild beasts of the field that are in Lebanon will come; and the wild beasts came and trampled down the achouch.
verses.25:19: You said, 'Look, you struck down Idumea,' and your heavy heart lifts you up. Now stay in your house; and why do you engage in harm, and you will fall, you and Judah with you?"
verses.25:20: And Amaziah did not listen, because it came about from the Lord to deliver him into hands, because he sought out the gods of the Idumeans.
verses.25:21: And Joash king of Israel went up, and they faced one another, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
verses.25:22: And Judah was routed before Israel, and each fled to his tent.
verses.25:23: And Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, at Beth-shemesh, and brought them into Jerusalem, and tore down four hundred cubits of the wall of Jerusalem, from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate.
verses.25:24: And all the gold and the silver and all the vessels found in the house of the Lord and with Jabdedom, and the treasures of the king's house, and the sons of the mixtures; and he returned to Samaria.
verses.25:25: And Amaziah the son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after Joash the son of Joash, king of Israel, died.
verses.25:26: And the rest of the acts of Amaziah, the first and the last, look, are they not written in the book of Judah and Israel?
verses.25:27: And at the time when Amaziah turned away from the Lord, they laid a plot against him, and he fled from Jerusalem to Lachish; and they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
verses.25:28: And they carried him up on the horses, and buried him with his fathers in the city of David.
verses.26:1: And all the people of the land took Ahaziah, and he was sixteen years old, and they made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.26:2: He built Elath; he restored it to Judah after the king slept with his fathers.
verses.26:3: Uzziah was sixteen years old, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Chaaia from Jerusalem.
verses.26:4: And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.
verses.26:5: And he kept seeking the Lord in all the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the fear of the Lord; and in his days he sought the Lord, and the Lord prospered him.
verses.26:6: And he went out and waged war against the foreigners, and tore down the walls of Gath and the walls of Abenner and the walls of Ashdod, and built cities of Ashdod and among the foreigners.
verses.26:7: And the Lord strengthened him against the foreigners, and against the Arabs who dwell upon the rock, and against the Minaeans.
verses.26:8: And the Minaeans gave gifts to Uzziah, and his name reached as far as the entrance of Egypt, because he grew strong to the highest degree.
verses.26:9: And Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem, both at the Corner Gate and at the gate of the corner of the valley and at the corners, and he grew strong.
verses.26:10: And he built towers in the wilderness, and hewed out many cisterns, because he had much livestock in the Shephelah and in the plain, and vinedressers in the hill country and in Carmel, because he was a farmer.
verses.26:11: And Uzziah had forces that waged war and went out to battle array by number; and their number was by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Amasaiah the judge, by the hand of Hananiah, the deputy of the king.
verses.26:12: The whole number of the patriarchs of those mighty for war was two thousand six hundred,
verses.26:13: and with them a fighting force of three hundred seven thousand five hundred; these were the ones who waged war with mighty strength to help the king against the adversaries.
verses.26:14: And Uzziah prepared them for the whole army: shields and spears and helmets and breastplates and bows and slings for stones.
verses.26:15: And he made in Jerusalem machines devised by a designer, to be on the towers and on the corners, to shoot arrows and large stones; and their construction was heard of far away, because he was marvelously helped until he grew strong.
verses.26:16: And when he grew strong, his heart was lifted up to bring ruin; and he did wrong against the Lord his God, and entered the temple of the Lord to burn incense on the altar of incense.
verses.26:17: And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of the Lord, mighty men.
verses.26:18: And they stood against Uzziah the king and said to him, "It is not for you, Uzziah, to offer sacrifice to the Lord, but rather for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who have been consecrated to offer sacrifice. Go out from the sanctuary, because you have turned away from the Lord; and this will not be for glory to you from the Lord God."
verses.26:19: And Uzziah became angry, and in his hand was the censer to burn incense in the temple; and while he was angry with the priests, leprosy sprang up on his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord and above the altar of incense.
verses.26:20: And the chief priest and the priests turned toward him, and look, he was leprous on his forehead; and they hurried him out from there, and indeed he himself hurried to go out, because the Lord had rebuked him.
verses.26:21: And King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death, and he lived as a leper in a house of apphousion, because he was cut off from the house of the Lord; and Jotham his son was over his kingdom, judging the people of the land.
verses.26:22: And the rest of the acts of Uzziah, the first and the last, are written by Jesseiah the prophet.
verses.26:23: And Uzziah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the burial of the kings, because they said, "He is a leper." And Jotham his son became king in his place.
verses.27:1: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Jerusha, the daughter of Sador.
verses.27:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that Uzziah his father had done, yet he did not enter the temple of the Lord; and the people were still corrupting themselves.
verses.27:3: He built the high gate of the house of the Lord, and on its wall Opla he built much,
verses.27:4: in the mountain of Judah and in the forests, both dwellings and towers.
verses.27:5: He fought against the king of the sons of Ammon and prevailed over him. And they gave him each year one hundred talents of silver, and ten thousand kors of wheat, and ten thousand of barley; these the king of Ammon brought to him each year, in the first year, and the second, and the third.
verses.27:6: And Jotham grew strong, because he prepared his ways before the Lord his God.
verses.27:7: And the rest of the acts of Jotham, and the war, and his deeds, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.27:9: And Jotham slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David; and Ahaz his son became king in his place.
verses.28:1: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And he did not do what was right before the Lord, like David his father.
verses.28:2: And he walked according to the ways of the king of Israel, for he also made carved images among their idols.
verses.28:3: He sacrificed in Gaibenthom and led his children through fire, and the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had utterly destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.28:4: And he burned incense on the high places and on the rooftops and beneath every leafy tree.
verses.28:5: And the Lord his God delivered him into the hand of the kings of Syria, and He struck him, and they took a great number of captives from them. Indeed, He also delivered him into the hands of the kings of Israel, and he struck himself with a great blow.
verses.28:6: And Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, sent in Judah in one day one hundred twenty thousand men mighty in strength, because they had forsaken the Lord, the God of their fathers.
verses.28:7: And Zichri, the mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the son of the king, and Azrikam, ruler of his house, and Elkanah, the successor of the king.
verses.28:8: And the sons of Israel took captive from their brothers three hundred thousand: women, sons, and daughters; and they plundered much plunder from them, and brought the plunder to Samaria.
verses.28:9: And there was the prophet of the Lord, Oded by name; and he went out to meet the army of those coming to Samaria and said to them, "Look, the wrath of the Lord, the God of your fathers, was upon Judah, and He delivered them into your hands, and you killed among them in wrath; it has reached as far as the heavens.
verses.28:10: And now you say you will take possession of the sons of Judah and Jerusalem as male slaves and female slaves. Look, is it not for you with yourselves to bear witness to the Lord our God?
verses.28:11: And now listen to me and return the captives of your brothers whom you took captive, because the wrath of the Lord is upon you."
verses.28:12: And leaders from the sons of Ephraim stood up, Udeia the son of Johanan, and Zechariah the son of Meshillemoth, and Hezekiah the son of Shallum, and Amasiah the son of Choad, against those coming from the war,
verses.28:13: and said to them, "You must by no means bring the captives here to us, for you speak of sinning against the Lord upon us, to add to our sins and to the ignorance; for our sin is great, and the wrath of the Lord God is upon Israel."
verses.28:14: And the warriors left the captives and the plunder before the leaders and all the assembly.
verses.28:15: And men who were called by name stood up and helped the captives, and clothed all the naked ones from the plunder; they dressed them and put sandals on them, and gave them both to eat and to anoint themselves, and also helped every weak one on pack animals, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brothers; and they returned to Samaria.
verses.28:16: At that time Ahaz sent to the king of Assyria to help him,
verses.28:17: and in this also, because the Idumeans had attacked and struck in Judah and taken captives.
verses.28:18: And the foreigners attacked the cities of the lowland and on the south of Judah, and they captured Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, and Galero, and Soco and its villages, and Galezo and its villages; and they settled there.
verses.28:19: For the Lord humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Judah, because he had turned away in rebellion from the Lord.
verses.28:20: And Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came against him, and they afflicted him.
verses.28:21: And Ahaz took the things in the house of the Lord and the things in the house of the king and of the leaders, and gave them to the king of Assyria; yet it was not for their help,
verses.28:22: but only for his affliction. And he went on even more to turn away from the Lord, and the king said,
verses.28:23: "I will seek the gods of Damascus who strike me." And he said, "The gods of the king of Syria, they will strengthen them; therefore I will sacrifice to them, and they will help me." And they became a stumbling block to him and to all Israel.
verses.28:24: And Ahaz removed the vessels of the house of the Lord and cut them in pieces, and shut the doors of the house of the Lord, and made for himself altars in every corner,
verses.28:25: and in every single city in Judah he made high places to burn incense to foreign gods; and they provoked the Lord, the God of their fathers, to anger.
verses.28:26: And the rest of his matters and his deeds, the first and the last, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.28:27: And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and he was buried in the city of David, for they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. And Hezekiah his son became king in his place.
verses.29:1: And Hezekiah became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Abba, the daughter of Zechariah.
verses.29:2: And he did what was right before the Lord, according to all that David his father had done.
verses.29:3: And it happened, when he stood over his kingdom, in the first month he opened the doors of the house of the Lord and repaired them.
verses.29:4: And he brought in the priests and the Levites, and stationed them on the side toward the east,
verses.29:5: and said to them, "Listen, Levites! Now purify yourselves, and purify the house of the Lord, the God of your fathers, and cast out the uncleanness from the sanctuary.
verses.29:6: For our fathers turned away and did what was evil before the Lord and forsook Him, and they turned their face away from the tabernacle of the Lord and gave the back of the neck.
verses.29:7: They also shut the doors of the temple, and put out the lamps, and did not burn incense, and did not offer burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
verses.29:8: And the Lord was angry with wrath against Judah and Jerusalem, and He gave them over to astonishment and to hissing, as you yourselves see with your eyes.
verses.29:9: And look, your fathers have been struck down by the sword, and your sons and your daughters and your wives are in captivity in a land not their own, which is so even now.
verses.29:10: Because of these things, it is now upon the heart to make my covenant, a covenant of the Lord, the God of Israel; and He has turned away the wrath of His fury from us.
verses.29:11: And now do not be negligent, for He has chosen you to stand before Him to minister, and to be ministering and burning incense to Him."
verses.29:12: And the Levites stood up: Mahath the son of Masi and Joel the son of Zechariah from the sons of Kohath; and from the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi and Zechariah the son of Helle; and from the sons of Gershon, from Zimmah and Jodan, these were sons of Joah;
verses.29:13: and of the sons of Elizaphan, both Zimri and Jeiel; and of the sons of Asa, Azariah and Mattaniah;
verses.29:14: and of the sons of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
verses.29:15: And he gathered their brothers, and they purified themselves according to the command of the king by the decree of the Lord.
verses.29:16: And the priests went all the way into the house of the Lord to purify it, and they cast out all the uncleanness that was found in the house of the Lord, even into the courtyard of the house of the Lord; and the Levites received it to cast it out into the brook Kidron outside.
verses.29:17: And they began to purify on the third day, the new moon of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they entered into the temple of the Lord, and they purified the house of the Lord in eight days, and on the thirteenth day of the first month they finished.
verses.29:18: And they went inside to Hezekiah the king and said, "We have purified all the things in the house of the Lord, the altar of the burnt offering and its vessels, and the table of the presentation and its vessels,
verses.29:19: and all the vessels that Ahaz the king defiled in his reign in his rebellion, we have prepared and purified; look, they are before the altar of the Lord."
verses.29:20: And Hezekiah the king rose early and gathered the leaders of the city, and went up to the house of the Lord.
verses.29:21: And he brought up seven young bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for a sin offering, for the kingdom and for the sanctuary and for Israel; and he told the sons of Aaron, the priests, to go up onto the altar of the Lord.
verses.29:22: And they slaughtered the young bulls, and the priests received the blood and poured it out upon the altar; and they slaughtered the rams, and poured the blood out upon the altar.
verses.29:23: And they brought forward the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.
verses.29:24: And the priests slaughtered them, and made atonement with their blood at the altar, and made atonement for all Israel; for, "For all Israel," the king said, "are the burnt offering and the sin offerings."
verses.29:25: And he stationed the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals and with harps and with lyres, according to the command of David the king, and of Gad the prophet, and of Nathan the prophet; for the decree was by the command of the Lord through the hand of the prophets.
verses.29:26: And the Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.
verses.29:27: And Hezekiah gave word to offer the burnt offering upon the altar. And when they began to offer the burnt offering, they began to sing to the Lord, along with trumpets to the accompaniment of the instruments of David the king.
verses.29:28: And the whole assembly was worshiping, and the singers were singing, and the trumpets were sounding, until the burnt offering was finished.
verses.29:29: And when they finished offering, the king and all who were present bowed down and worshiped.
verses.29:30: And Hezekiah the king and the leaders told the Levites to sing praise to the Lord in the words of David and of Asaph the prophet. And they sang praise with gladness, and they fell down and worshiped.
verses.29:31: And Hezekiah answered and said, "Now you have filled your hands to the Lord; come near and bring sacrifices and offerings of praise to the house of the Lord." And the assembly brought sacrifices and offerings of praise to the house of the Lord, and everyone willing in heart, burnt offerings.
verses.29:32: And the number of the burnt offering that the assembly brought was seventy young bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs; all these were for a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.29:33: And the consecrated young bulls were six hundred, and sheep, three thousand five hundred.
verses.29:34: However, the priests were few and were not able to skin the burnt offering; so their brothers the Levites helped them until the work was finished and until the priests had purified themselves, because the Levites purified themselves more eagerly than the priests.
verses.29:35: And the burnt offering was abundant, with the fat pieces of the completion of the peace offering and the drink offerings of the burnt offering. And the work in the house of the Lord was set in order.
verses.29:36: And Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced because God had made preparation for the people, for the matter came about suddenly.
verses.30:1: And Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and he wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh to come to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem to observe the Passover to the Lord God of Israel.
verses.30:2: And the king and the officials and all the assembly in Jerusalem took counsel to observe the Passover in the second month.
verses.30:3: For they were not able to observe it at that time, because the priests had not been purified in sufficient number, and the people had not been gathered to Jerusalem.
verses.30:4: And the matter was pleasing before the king and before the assembly.
verses.30:5: And they established a decree for a proclamation to go throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that they should come to observe the Passover to the Lord God of Israel in Jerusalem, because a multitude had not observed it according to what was written.
verses.30:6: And the runners went with the letters from the king and the officials into all Israel and Judah, according to the command of the king, saying, "Sons of Israel, return to the God of Abraham and Isaac and Israel, and bring back those who have been rescued, who were left from the hand of the king of Assyria.
verses.30:7: And do not become like your fathers and your brothers, who departed from the Lord, the God of their fathers, and He gave them over to desolation, just as you see.
verses.30:8: And now do not harden your hearts; give glory to the Lord God, and enter into His sanctuary, which He consecrated forever, and serve the Lord your God, and He will turn away from you the fury of wrath.
verses.30:9: For when you return to the Lord, your brothers and your children will find compassion before all who took them captive, and He will bring them back to this land; for the Lord our God is merciful and compassionate, and He will not turn His face away from you, if we return to Him."
verses.30:10: And the runners were passing from city to city in the hill country of Ephraim and Manasseh, and as far as Zebulun; but they were like those laughing at and mocking them.
verses.30:11: Yet men of Asher and from Manasseh and from Zebulun turned and came to Jerusalem and into Judah.
verses.30:12: And the hand of the Lord came to give them one heart, to come to act according to the commands of the king and the officials by the word of the Lord.
verses.30:13: And many people were gathered to Jerusalem to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month, a very large assembly.
verses.30:14: And they rose up and removed the altars that were in Jerusalem, and everything on which they burned incense to the false ones they tore down and threw into the brook Kidron.
verses.30:15: And they slaughtered the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month; and the priests and the Levites were ashamed and purified themselves, and they brought burnt offerings into the house of the Lord.
verses.30:16: And they stood at their station according to their ordinance, according to the commandment of Moses, the man of God, and the priests were receiving the blood from the hand of the Levites.
verses.30:17: For a multitude of the assembly had not been purified, and the Levites were to slaughter the Passover for everyone who was not able to be purified to the Lord.
verses.30:18: For most of the people from Ephraim and Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun had not purified themselves, yet they ate this Passover contrary to what was written. And Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May the good Lord make atonement
verses.30:19: for every heart that directs itself to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, though not according to the purification of the sanctuary."
verses.30:20: And the Lord heard Hezekiah and healed the people.
verses.30:21: And the sons of Israel who were found in Jerusalem observed the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great gladness, singing hymns to the Lord day by day, and the priests and the Levites with instruments to the Lord.
verses.30:22: And Hezekiah spoke to the heart of all the Levites and of those who showed good understanding for the Lord; and they completed the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days, sacrificing sacrifices of deliverance and giving thanks to the Lord, the God of their fathers.
verses.30:23: And the assembly took counsel together to observe seven more days; and they observed seven days with gladness.
verses.30:24: For Hezekiah presented as an offering to Judah, to the assembly, a thousand calves and seven thousand sheep; and the officials presented as an offering to the people a thousand calves and ten thousand sheep, and the holy things of the priests in abundance.
verses.30:25: And all the assembly rejoiced, the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly of Judah, and those who were found from Israel, and the proselytes who came in from the land of Israel and those dwelling from Judah.
verses.30:26: And there was great gladness in Jerusalem; from the days of Solomon son of David, king of Israel, there had not been such a feast in Jerusalem.
verses.30:27: And the priests, the Levites, rose up and blessed the people; and their voice was heard, and their prayer came to His holy dwelling place, to heaven.
verses.31:1: And when all these things were completed, all Israel who were found in the cities of Judah went out and shattered the pillars and cut down the groves and tore down the high places and the altars from all the land of Judea and Benjamin and Ephraim and from Manasseh to completion; and all Israel returned, each one to his inheritance and to their cities.
verses.31:2: And Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites, and the divisions of each one according to his own service, for the priests and for the Levites, for the burnt offering and for the sacrifice of deliverance, and to praise and to give thanks and to serve in the gates, in the courts of the house of the Lord.
verses.31:3: And the king's portion from his possessions was for the burnt offerings, the morning and the evening, and burnt offerings for Sabbaths and for the new moons and for the feasts written in the law of the Lord.
verses.31:4: And they told the people dwelling in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, so that they might be strong in the service of the house of the Lord.
verses.31:5: And when he commanded the matter, Israel abundantly gave firstfruits of grain and wine and oil and honey and all the produce of the field. And the sons of Israel and Judah brought all the tithes in abundance.
verses.31:6: And those dwelling in the cities of Judah, they also brought tithes of calves and sheep and tithes of goats, and consecrated them to the Lord their God, and brought them in and placed them in heaps.
verses.31:7: In the third month the foundation heaps began to be laid, and in the seventh month they were completed.
verses.31:8: And Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, and they blessed the Lord and His people Israel.
verses.31:9: And Hezekiah inquired of the priests and the Levites concerning the heaps.
verses.31:10: And Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, spoke and said, "Since the firstfruits began to be brought into the house of the Lord, we have eaten and drunk and left some over; for the Lord has blessed His people, and we have left over up to this abundance."
verses.31:11: And Hezekiah gave orders to prepare chambers in the house of the Lord. And they prepared them.
verses.31:12: And they brought the firstfruits and the tithes there in faithfulness, and over them as overseer was Chomenias the Levite, and Shimei his brother was second in command.
verses.31:13: And Eiel and Uzziah and Mahath and Asahel and Jerimoth and Ezabath and Jeiel and Samachiah and Thanai, Benaiah and his sons, were appointed through Conaniah and Shimei his brother, just as King Hezekiah and Azariah the ruler of the house of the Lord commanded.
verses.31:14: And Kore the son of Heman the Levite, the gatekeeper toward the east, was over the gifts, to give the firstfruits to the Lord and the most holy things,
verses.31:15: by the hand of Odom and Benjamin and Jeshua and Shimei and Marias and Shecaniah, by the hand of the priests in faithfulness, to give to their brothers according to the divisions, both the great and the small,
verses.31:16: each one of the offspring of the males from three years old and upward, to everyone entering the house of the Lord, for the daily reckoning day by day, for service in the divisions of their order.
verses.31:17: This was the enrollment of the priests by fathers' houses, and the Levites in their divisions from twenty years old and upward in order,
verses.31:18: to enroll them with all the offspring of their sons and their daughters, for the whole multitude, because in faithfulness they purified what is holy.
verses.31:19: For the sons of Aaron who served as priests, and those from their cities, in every single city there were men who were named by name to give a portion to every male among the priests and to everyone numbered among the Levites.
verses.31:20: And Hezekiah did so throughout all Judah, and he did what was good and what was upright before the Lord his God.
verses.31:21: And in every work that he began in labor in the house of the Lord, and in the law and in the commands, he sought his God with all his soul, and he acted and prospered.
verses.32:1: And after these matters and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came, and he came against Judah and encamped against the walled cities, and said he would seize them.
verses.32:2: And Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and that his face was set to wage war against Jerusalem.
verses.32:3: And he took counsel with his elders and the mighty men to stop up the waters of the springs that were outside the city; and he supported him.
verses.32:4: And he gathered many people and stopped up the waters of the springs and the river that divides through the city, saying, "May the king of Assyria not come and find much water and grow strong."
verses.32:5: And Hezekiah grew strong and built all the wall that had been torn down, and towers, and another bulwark outside, and he strengthened the embankment of the city of David, and he made many weapons.
verses.32:6: And he appointed commanders of war over the people, and they were gathered to him at the square of the gate of the valley, and he spoke to their heart, saying,
verses.32:7: "Be strong and be courageous; do not be terrified before the king of Assyria and before all the nation that is with him, for there are more with us than with him.
verses.32:8: With him are arms of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God, to save and to wage our war." And the people took courage at the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
verses.32:9: And after these things, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians sent his servants to Jerusalem, while he himself was against Lachish and all the army was with him, and he sent to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah who were in Jerusalem, saying,
verses.32:10: "Thus says the king of the Assyrians: In what are you trusting? Will you sit under siege in Jerusalem?
verses.32:11: Is Hezekiah not deceiving you to hand you over to death and to famine and to thirst, saying, 'The Lord our God will save you from the hand of the king of Assyria'?
verses.32:12: This is Hezekiah, who removed His altars and His high places, and spoke to Judah and to those dwelling in Jerusalem, saying, 'Before this altar you shall worship, and on it you shall burn incense.'
verses.32:13: Will you not know what I and my fathers did to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of all the earth at all able to save their people from my hand?
verses.32:14: Who was there among all the gods of these nations that my fathers utterly destroyed? Were they able to save their people from my hand, that your God will be able to save you from my hand?
verses.32:15: Now do not let Hezekiah deceive you, and do not let him make you trust in this way, and do not believe him; for no god of any nation or kingdom will by any means be able to save his people from my hand and from the hand of my fathers, for your God will by no means save you from my hand."
verses.32:16: And his servants spoke still further against the Lord God and against Hezekiah His servant.
verses.32:17: And he wrote a letter to revile the Lord God of Israel, and spoke about Him, saying, "Just as the gods of the nations of the earth did not deliver their peoples from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will by no means deliver His people from my hand."
verses.32:18: And he shouted with a loud voice in the language of Judah to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to help them and to pull down, so that they might seize the city.
verses.32:19: And he spoke against the God of Jerusalem just as also against the gods of the peoples of the earth, works of the hands of men.
verses.32:20: And Hezekiah the king and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet prayed about these things and cried out to heaven.
verses.32:21: And the Lord sent an angel; he wiped out every mighty man and warrior and commander and general in the camp of the king of Assyria, and he returned with shame of face to his own land. And he went into the house of his god, and some of those who came out from his own body struck him down with the sword.
verses.32:22: And the Lord saved Hezekiah and those dwelling in Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all, and He gave them rest all around.
verses.32:23: And many brought gifts to the Lord to Jerusalem and presents to Hezekiah king of Judah, and he was highly exalted in the eyes of all the nations after these things.
verses.32:24: In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death, and he prayed to the Lord, and He heard him and gave him a sign.
verses.32:25: And Hezekiah did not repay according to the benefit that He gave him, but his heart was lifted up; and wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.32:26: And Hezekiah humbled himself from the loftiness of his heart, along with those dwelling in Jerusalem, and the wrath of God did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.
verses.32:27: And Hezekiah had very great wealth and glory; and he made for himself treasuries of silver and gold and precious stone, and for spices, and armories, and for desirable vessels,
verses.32:28: and cities for the produce of grain and oil and wine, and stalls for every kind of livestock, and folds for the flocks,
verses.32:29: and cities that he built for himself, and possessions of sheep and cattle in abundance, for the Lord gave him very great possessions.
verses.32:30: Hezekiah himself stopped up the outlet of the upper water of Zion, and directed it down to the west of the city of David; and Hezekiah prospered in all his works.
verses.32:31: And so, concerning the envoys of the rulers from Babylon who were sent to him to inquire from him about the wonder that had happened in the land, the Lord left him to test him, to know what was in his heart.
verses.32:32: And the rest of the deeds of Hezekiah and his mercy, see, they are written in the prophecy of Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet and in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.32:33: And Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David; and all Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem gave him glory and honor at his death; and Manasseh his son reigned in his place.
verses.33:1: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
verses.33:2: And he did what was evil before the Lord, from among all the abominations of the nations whom the Lord utterly destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.33:3: And he turned back and built the high places that Hezekiah his father had torn down, and he set up pillars for the Baals and made groves, and he worshiped all the host of heaven and served them.
verses.33:4: And he built altars in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord said, "In Jerusalem My name shall be forever."
verses.33:5: And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.
verses.33:6: And he himself led his children through fire in Ge-bene-Hinnom; and he practiced soothsaying and practiced sorcery and read omens, and he appointed mediums and enchanters; he multiplied doing what was evil before the Lord, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.33:7: And he placed the carved, cast image, a likeness that he made, in the house of God, of which God said to David and Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will place My name forever.
verses.33:8: And I will not again move the foot of Israel from the land that I gave to their fathers, only if they are careful to do all that I commanded them, according to all the law, the statutes, and the ordinances by the hand of Moses."
verses.33:9: And Manasseh led Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem astray, to do what was evil beyond all the nations that the Lord removed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.33:10: And the Lord spoke to Manasseh and to his people, and he did not listen.
verses.33:11: And the Lord brought against them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, and they captured Manasseh in bonds and bound him in fetters and brought him to Babylon.
verses.33:12: And when he was in distress, he sought the face of the Lord his God, and he humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers;
verses.33:13: and he prayed to Him, and He heard him, and He heard his cry, and He brought him back to Jerusalem to his kingdom; and Manasseh knew that the Lord Himself is God.
verses.33:14: And after these things he built a wall outside the city of David on the west toward Gihon in the torrent valley, and as one goes out through the surrounding gate, and up to Ophel itself, and he raised it very high; and he stationed commanders of the army in all the walled cities in Judah.
verses.33:15: And he removed the foreign gods and the carved image from the house of the Lord, and all the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of the Lord and in Jerusalem and outside the city.
verses.33:16: And he restored the altar of the Lord, and he sacrificed on it a sacrifice of deliverance and praise, and he told Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.
verses.33:17: Yet the people were still on the high places; yet the Lord was their God.
verses.33:18: And the rest of the deeds of Manasseh, and his prayer to God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the God of Israel,
verses.33:19: see, they are in the words of his prayer, and He heard him; and all his sins and his rebellions, and the places on which he built the high places and set up there groves and carved images before he turned back, see, they are written in the words of the seers.
verses.33:20: And Manasseh slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the garden of his house; and Amos his son reigned in his place.
verses.33:21: Amos was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
verses.33:22: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, as Manasseh his father had done; and Amos sacrificed to all the idols that Manasseh his father had made, and he served them.
verses.33:23: And he did not humble himself before the Lord as Manasseh his father had humbled himself, for his son Amos multiplied guilt.
verses.33:24: And his servants plotted against him and struck him down in his house.
verses.33:25: And the people of the land struck down those who had plotted against King Amos; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
verses.34:1: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
verses.34:2: And he did what was right before the Lord, and walked in the ways of David his father, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.34:3: And in the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a youth, he began to seek the Lord, the God of David his father; and in the twelfth year of his reign he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem from the high places and the groves, and from the cast images.
verses.34:4: And he tore down the altars of the Baals that were before him and the high places that were above them, and he cut down the groves and the carved images, and he broke in pieces and ground fine the cast images and threw them upon the surface of the tombs of those who sacrificed to them.
verses.34:5: And he burned the bones of priests upon the altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem,
verses.34:6: and in the cities of Ephraim and Manasseh and Simeon and Naphtali, and in their places all around.
verses.34:7: And he tore down the groves and the altars, and chopped the idols into fine pieces, and cut down all the high places from all the land of Israel, and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.34:8: And in the eighteenth year of his reign, to cleanse the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Selia, and Maasa the ruler of the city, and Juach son of Joah his recorder, to strengthen the house of the Lord his God.
verses.34:9: And they came to Hilkiah the high priest and gave the silver that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites guarding the gate had collected from the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim and the rulers, and from all the remnant in Israel, and from the sons of Judah and Benjamin, and from those living in Jerusalem.
verses.34:10: And they gave it into the hand of those doing the work who were appointed in the house of the Lord, and they gave it to those doing the work who were working in the house of the Lord, to repair and strengthen the house.
verses.34:11: And they gave it to the carpenters and to the builders, to buy squared stones and timber for beams, to roof the houses that the kings of Judah had destroyed.
verses.34:12: And the men were faithful over the work, and over them as overseers were Ie and Obadiah, the Levites from the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the sons of Kohath, to oversee, and every Levite, everyone skilled with instruments of song.
verses.34:13: And they were over the burden-bearers and over all those doing the work, task by task; and from the Levites there were scribes and judges and gatekeepers.
verses.34:14: And while they were bringing out the silver that had been brought into the house of the Lord, Hilkiah the priest found a book of the law of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
verses.34:15: And Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found a book of the law in the house of the Lord." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
verses.34:16: And Shaphan brought the book to the king, and further brought back word to the king: "All the silver that was given is in the hand of your servants who are doing the work.
verses.34:17: And they melted down the silver that was found in the house of the Lord, and he gave it into the hand of the overseers who do the work."
verses.34:18: And Shaphan the scribe reported to the king, saying, "A book that Hilkiah the priest gave me." And Shaphan read it before the king.
verses.34:19: And it happened, when the king heard the law, that he tore his garments.
verses.34:20: And the king commanded Hilkiah, and Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Abdodom son of Micah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Isaiah the servant of the king, saying,
verses.34:21: "Go, inquire of the Lord concerning me and concerning all that is left in Israel and Judah, concerning the words of the book that has been found; for great is the wrath of the Lord that has been kindled among us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of the Lord to do according to all that is written in this book."
verses.34:22: And Hilkiah and those to whom the king had spoken went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum son of Kathual son of Chelles, who kept the commandments; and she lived in Jerusalem in Maasanai. And they spoke to her according to these things.
verses.34:23: And she said to them, "Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to Me,
verses.34:24: 'Thus says the Lord: Look, I am bringing evils upon this place, all the words that are written in the book that has been read before the king of Judah,
verses.34:25: because they forsook Me and burned incense to foreign gods, so that they might provoke Me to anger with all the works of their hands; and My wrath has been kindled in this place and will not be quenched.'
verses.34:26: And to the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of the Lord, thus you shall say to him: 'Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: As for the words that you heard,
verses.34:27: and your heart was contrite, and you humbled yourself before My face when you heard My words against this place and against those who live in it, and you humbled yourself before Me and tore your garments and wept in My presence, and I also have heard, says the Lord.
verses.34:28: Look, I am gathering you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your tombs in peace, and your eyes will not look upon all the evils that I am bringing upon this place and upon those who live in it.'" And they brought back word to the king.
verses.34:29: And the king sent and gathered the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.34:30: And the king went up to the house of the Lord, and all Judah and those living in Jerusalem, and the priests and the Levites and all the people, from great to small; and he read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that were found in the house of the Lord.
verses.34:31: And the king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk before the Lord, to keep His commandments and testimonies and His statutes with a whole heart and with a whole soul, the words of the covenant that are written in this book.
verses.34:32: And he caused all who were found in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand; and those living in Jerusalem made a covenant in the house of the Lord, the God of their father.
verses.34:33: And Josiah removed all the abominations from all the land that belonged to the sons of Israel, and made all who were found in Jerusalem and in Israel serve the Lord their God all his days; he did not turn aside from following the Lord, the God of his fathers.
verses.35:1: And Josiah kept the Passover to the Lord his God; and they sacrificed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.35:2: And he appointed the priests to their duties and strengthened them for the work of the house of the Lord.
verses.35:3: And he told the Levites who were capable in all Israel to consecrate themselves to the Lord; and they placed the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David, the king of Israel, had built. And the king said, "You are not to carry anything on your shoulders; now therefore minister to the Lord your God and to His people Israel,
verses.35:4: and prepare yourselves according to your ancestral houses and according to your courses, according to the writing of David king of Israel and by the hand of King Solomon his son;
verses.35:5: and stand in the house according to the divisions of your ancestral houses for your brothers, the sons of the people, and a portion of an ancestral house for the Levites;
verses.35:6: and sacrifice the Passover, and prepare for your brothers, to do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses."
verses.35:7: And Josiah contributed to the sons of the people sheep and lambs and kids from the young of the goats, all that were for the Passover, and all those found to the number of thirty thousand, and three thousand calves; these were from the possessions of the king.
verses.35:8: And his rulers contributed to the people and to the priests and Levites; Hilkiah and Zechariah and Jehiel, the rulers of the house of God, gave to the priests, and they gave for the Passover two thousand six hundred sheep and lambs and kids, and three hundred calves.
verses.35:9: And Conaniah and Benaiah and Shemaiah and Nethanel his brother, and Hashabiah and Joel and Jozabad, rulers of the Levites, contributed to the Levites for the Passover five thousand, and five hundred calves.
verses.35:10: And the ministry was set in order, and the priests stood at their station and the Levites in their divisions, according to the command of the king.
verses.35:11: And they sacrificed the Passover, and the priests poured out the blood from their hand, and the Levites skinned them.
verses.35:12: And they prepared the burnt offering to hand it over to them according to the division by ancestral houses for the sons of the people, to offer to the Lord, as it is written in the book of Moses; and so until the morning.
verses.35:13: And they roasted the Passover in fire according to the ordinance, and they boiled the holy offerings in the bronze pots and in the cauldrons; and it went well, and they ran to all the sons of the people.
verses.35:14: And after preparing for them and for the priests, because the priests were offering up the fat portions and the burnt offerings until night, the Levites prepared for themselves and for their brothers, the sons of Aaron.
verses.35:15: And the singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their station according to the commands of David, and Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun, the prophets of the king; and the rulers and the gatekeepers, gate by gate, did not have to move from the ministry of the holy things, for their brothers the Levites prepared for them.
verses.35:16: And all the ministry of the Lord was set in order and prepared on that day, to keep the Passover and to offer the burnt offerings upon the altar of the Lord, according to the command of King Josiah.
verses.35:17: And the sons of Israel who were found kept the Passover at that time, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
verses.35:18: And there had not been a Passover like it in Israel; from the days of Samuel the prophet and of every king of Israel they had not kept one like the Passover that Josiah and the priests and the Levites and all Judah and the Israel that was found and those living in Jerusalem kept to the Lord,
verses.35:19: in the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah. And the mediums and the spiritists and the teraphim and the idols and the karaseim that were in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, King Josiah burned with fire, so that he might establish the words of the law that were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the Lord. There was no one like him before him who turned to the Lord with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength according to all the law of Moses, and after him no one like him arose. Yet the Lord did not turn from the anger of His great wrath, with which the Lord was angered in wrath against Judah because of all the statutes with which Manasseh provoked Him to anger. And the Lord said, "I will also remove Judah from sight, just as I removed Israel, and I have rejected the city that I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name will be there.'"
verses.35:20: And Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians at the Euphrates River, and King Josiah went to meet him.
verses.35:21: And he sent messengers to him, saying, "What is there between me and you, king of Judah? And I have not come against you today to wage war; and God has told me to hurry. Watch out for God who is with me, so that He may not destroy you."
verses.35:22: And Josiah did not turn his face away from him, but rather strengthened himself to fight against him, and did not listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God, and came to fight in the plain of Megiddo.
verses.35:23: And the archers shot at King Josiah; and the king said to his servants, "Take me out, for I am severely hurt."
verses.35:24: And his servants took him out of the chariot and put him up into the second chariot that he had, and they brought him to Jerusalem; and he died and was buried with his fathers. And all Judah and Jerusalem mourned over Josiah.
verses.35:25: And Jeremiah lamented over Josiah, and all the male and female rulers spoke a lament over Josiah until this day; and they made it a statute in Israel, and look, it is written in the Laments.
verses.35:26: And the acts of Josiah and his hope were written in the law of the Lord,
verses.35:27: and his acts, the first and the last, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
verses.36:1: And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, and they anointed him and appointed him as king in place of his father.
verses.36:2: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Abital, daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah. And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers did. And Pharaoh Neco bound him at Dablatha in the land of Hamath, so that he would not reign in Jerusalem.
verses.36:3: And the king removed him to Egypt, and he imposed a tribute on the land of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
verses.36:4: And Pharaoh Neco appointed Eliakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. And Pharaoh Neco took Jehoahaz his brother and brought him into Egypt, and he died there. And he gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh. Then the land began to be taxed in order to give the silver at the command of Pharaoh, and each one according to his ability exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Neco.
verses.36:5: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Zechora, daughter of Neriah, from Ramah. And he did what was evil before the Lord, according to everything that his fathers did. In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came into the land, and he served him three years, and rebelled against him. And the Lord sent against him the Chaldeans and raiding bands of Syrians and raiding bands of Moabites and of the sons of Ammon and of Samaria, and they departed after this word, according to the word of the Lord by the hand of His servants the prophets. Yet the wrath of the Lord was upon Judah, so that it would depart from His presence because of Manasseh, for all that he did, and for the innocent blood that Jehoiakim shed; he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood. And the Lord was not willing to destroy them.
verses.36:6: And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him, and bound him in bronze fetters and led him away to Babylon.
verses.36:7: And he carried off part of the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon, and placed them in his temple in Babylon.
verses.36:8: And the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and all that he did, look, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and was buried in Ganozae with his fathers. And Jeconiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.36:9: Jeconiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.36:10: And at the turn of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him into Babylon with the desirable vessels of the house of the Lord, and he made Zedekiah, his father's brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.36:11: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
verses.36:12: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord his God; he did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet and from the mouth of the Lord,
verses.36:13: by setting aside the matters with King Nebuchadnezzar that he had made him swear by God; and he stiffened his neck and fortified his heart so as not to return to the Lord, the God of Israel.
verses.36:14: And all the nobles of Judah and the priests and the people of the land increased in acting unfaithfully with the unfaithful deeds of the abominations of the nations, and they defiled the house of the Lord that was in Jerusalem.
verses.36:15: And the Lord God of their fathers sent out by hand, rising early and sending His messengers, because He was sparing His people and His sanctuary.
verses.36:16: And they were deriding His messengers and despising His words and mocking His prophets, until the wrath of the Lord rose up against His people, until there was no healing.
verses.36:17: And He brought against them the king of the Chaldeans, and he killed their young men with the sword in the house of His sanctuary; and he did not spare Zedekiah, and they had no mercy on their virgins, and they led away their older men. He handed everything over into their hands.
verses.36:18: And all the vessels of the house of God, the large and the small, and the treasures, and all the treasures of the king and of the high officials, he brought all of them into Babylon.
verses.36:19: And he burned the house of the Lord, and tore down the wall of Jerusalem, and burned its citadels with fire, and every beautiful vessel to destruction.
verses.36:20: And he exiled those who remained to Babylon, and they became servants to him and to his sons until the kingdom of the Medes,
verses.36:21: so that the word of the Lord through the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, until the land received its Sabbaths to keep Sabbath, to the completion of seventy years.
verses.36:22: In the first year of the king of the Persians, after the word of the Lord through the mouth of Jeremiah was fulfilled, the Lord roused the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he gave orders to proclaim throughout all his kingdom in writing, saying,
verses.36:23: "Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians to all the kingdoms of the earth: 'The Lord God of heaven has given to me, and He Himself has commanded me to build a house for Him in Jerusalem in Judea. Who among you is of all His people? His God will be with him, and let him go up.'"

notes.1:3: Greek reads "tent of testimony" (skene tou martyriou), the standard Septuagint rendering where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "tent of meeting."
notes.1:8: Greek opens Solomon's speech with the relative pronoun "what" (ho) rather than "You" (sy), likely an early scribal variant or an exclamatory construction.
notes.1:9: Greek reads "Your name" (to onoma sou), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Your word."
notes.1:13: Greek transliterates Hebrew bamah ("high place") as a place name, "Maba," and reads "which was in Jerusalem" where the Hebrew has "to Jerusalem."
notes.1:16: Greek reads "horsemen" (hippeon) rather than "horses," and renders the obscure Hebrew geographic term Kue as "price" (time) and "to go" (poreuesthai).
notes.2:3: "Continual presentation" (prothesin dia pantos) refers to the regular setting out of the bread of the Presence before the Lord.
notes.2:5: Greek reads "do not bear His glory," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "cannot contain Him."
notes.2:9: Greek renders Hebrew "crushed [wheat]" doubly as "for food" and "as gifts," and omits the twenty thousand measures of oil present in the Hebrew text (though oil is mentioned in 2:14).
notes.2:12: Greek renders the Hebrew title Huram-abi literally as "Hiram my father," where "father" functions as an honorific for a master craftsman.
notes.3:8: Greek reads "for cherubim, for six hundred talents," a doublet arising from reading Hebrew kikkarim ("talents") both as kerubim ("cherubim") and as "talents."
notes.3:11: Verse 3:12 of the Hebrew text, which describes the wings of the second cherub, is absent from the Greek text here.
notes.3:15: Greek reads "in front of the wall" (tou toichou) rather than "in front of the house" (tou oikou), likely through an inner-Greek scribal error.
notes.3:16: Greek retains the transliterated Hebrew architectural terms serseroth ("chains") and dabeir ("inner sanctuary"), just as it transliterates Hebrew ulam ("vestibule") as ailam in 3:4.
notes.3:17: Instead of transliterating the Hebrew pillar names Jachin and Boaz, the Greek translates their meanings as Katorthosis ("Establishment" or "Setting Upright") and Ischys ("Strength").
notes.4:5: The Greek noun rendered "measures" is the liquid unit metretes (about ten gallons each). The closing clause "and he finished" reflects a Septuagint reading of the Hebrew verb for "contain" as "finish."
notes.4:12: The Greek uses the Hebrew architectural loanwords golath ("globes") and chothareth ("capitals"), and reads "tops" instead of "two globes" in the second half; similarly, mechonoth ("stands") appears in 4:14 and dabeir ("inner sanctuary") in 4:20, 5:7, and 5:9.
notes.4:13: The Greek reads "four hundred golden bells" (where Hebrew has "pomegranates") and literally "kinds of pomegranates on the one network" (used distributively for "each network").
notes.4:17: The Greek reads "in the house of" (for Hebrew "between") and preserves the Septuagint-distinct place name Anamesirdathai, apparently formed by fusing Greek ana meson ("between") with Hebrew Zeredathah.
notes.4:22: The Greek links the second phrase with "to the golden doors" rather than a coordinating conjunction, and places the closing sentence ("And all the work...") at the end of 4:22, where Hebrew versification begins 5:1.
notes.5:6: The Greek adds "and those who feared" alongside "and those of them who were gathered together" and reverses the order to "calves and sheep."
notes.5:9: The Greek reads "from the holy place" (matching the phrasing in 5:11), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "from the ark."
notes.5:12: The Greek specifies "the sons of Asaph" (rather than "Asaph"), has singular "his sons and his brothers," and reads "opposite the altar" without "east."
notes.5:13: The Greek uses the neuter adjective "for it is good" (rather than masculine "for He is good") and ends with "a cloud of the glory of the Lord" (rather than "the house of the Lord").
notes.6:6: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Greek text does not include a clause about choosing Jerusalem here, moving directly to the choice of David.
notes.6:16: The Greek reads "in My name" (en to onomati mou) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "in my law," and has "from the presence" (apo prosopou) without a possessive pronoun.
notes.6:19: Throughout Solomon's prayer (6:19-39), the Greek uses future indicative verbs to render Hebrew petitionary weqatal forms; in 6:21, 25, 27, 39 (and 7:14), "pardon" translates the Septuagint idiom hileos eimi (lit. "be gracious/propitious").
notes.6:30: The Greek reads "and heal" (kai iase) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "and forgive," and in 6:31 reads "fear all Your ways" rather than "fear you, to walk in your ways."
notes.6:41: The Greek reads "Your sons" (hoi huioi sou) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "your faithful ones," and in 6:42 reads "Your face" (to prosopon sou) rather than "the face of your anointed one."
notes.7:3: The Greek uses the neuter adjective agathon ("For it is good") rather than the masculine "He is good."
notes.7:5: The Greek mentions only twenty-two thousand calves (lacking the 120,000 sheep of the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and links "and all the people" at the end of 7:5 directly into the standing clause of 7:6.
notes.7:7: "Grain offerings" translates ta manaa, the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew cultic term minhah.
notes.7:9: The Greek uses singular "he held" and describes a single seven-day festival for the dedication of the altar, without the additional seven-day period found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:13: The Greek reads to xylon (lit. "the tree/wood," i.e., "the trees") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "the land," and uses thanatos ("death," as in 6:28) idiomatically for deadly pestilence.
notes.8:3: Greek reads "Baisoba," a Septuagint place name corresponding to Hebrew "Hamath-zobah."
notes.8:4: Greek reads "fortified cities" here and in 8:6 where the Hebrew has "storage cities."
notes.8:8: Greek reads "with him" (rather than Hebrew "after them") and lacks a negative before "destroyed," reading "whom the sons of Israel destroyed" where the Hebrew reads "whom the sons of Israel had not destroyed."
notes.8:17: Greek reads "Elam" (Ailam), corresponding to Hebrew "Eloth" (Elath), and uses "Idumea," the Greek form for Edom.
notes.8:18: Greek reads "Sophira" (and "Suphir" in 9:10), the Septuagint forms corresponding to Hebrew "Ophir," and uses singular verbs ("went... took") before shifting to plural ("they came").
notes.9:4: Greek reads "the burnt offerings which he offered up in the house of the Lord" where the Hebrew reads "his ascent by which he went up to the house of the Lord."
notes.9:15: Greek preserves a textual doublet repeating the six hundred gold pieces for each large shield, whereas 9:16 omits the gold weight for the three hundred shields found in the Hebrew.
notes.9:24: Greek reads stakte ("myrrh") where the Hebrew has "weapons," and in 9:25 Greek reads "mares for chariots" rather than Hebrew "stalls for horses and chariots."
notes.9:26: Greek allophylon literally means "foreigners" and is the Septuagint's regular designation for the Philistines.
notes.9:29: Greek names the seer "Joel," differing from the Hebrew name "Iddo," and refers to "the words" of Ahijah rather than his "prophecy."
notes.10:11: Greek reads "our yoke" here and in 10:14 (reflecting a Greek pronoun interchange with "your yoke") and uses the verb "disciplined" for the yoke as well as the whips.
notes.10:15: Greek reads "saying" (introducing direct speech) where the Hebrew has "in order that," and continues the clause into 10:16 with the genitive "and all Israel" governed by "concerning."
notes.10:17: Greek reads "Jeroboam" (rather than Hebrew "Rehoboam") as the king who reigned over the men of Israel and those living in the cities of Judah.
notes.10:18: Greek reads "Adoniram" (matching 1 Kings 4:6; Hebrew 2 Chronicles has "Hadoram") and again reads "King Jeroboam" (rather than Hebrew "King Rehoboam") as the king who fled to Jerusalem.
notes.11:6: The Greek text reads "Bethseem" and "Apan" where the Hebrew has Bethlehem and Etam. Elsewhere in this city list (vv. 7-10), the Greek likewise preserves distinct forms: Succoth (Heb. Soco), Zib (Heb. Ziph), Adorai (Heb. Adoraim), and Aldon (Heb. Aijalon).
notes.11:16: The Greek reads "and he drove them out from the tribes of Israel," attributing the expulsion to Jeroboam, where the Hebrew reads "and after them from all the tribes of Israel."
notes.11:17: The Greek text shifts to singular verbs ("it strengthened" and "he walked") where other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew read plural verbs ("they strengthened" and "they walked").
notes.11:18: The Greek preserves distinct forms for these names: Mollath (Heb. Mahalath), Baia (Heb. Abihail, without a preceding "and"), and Elian (Heb. Eliab); similarly in vv. 19-20 it reads Jauth (Jeush), Roollam (Zaham), Jeththi (Attai), and Emmoth (Shelomith).
notes.11:21: The Greek reads "thirty concubines" where the Hebrew has sixty. In v. 23, the Greek also diverges notably, reading "he grew great beyond all his sons" and feminine "them" (referring to the fortified cities) as recipients of provisions.
notes.12:3: The Greek reads "sixty thousand horses" (Heb. horsemen) and "Troglodytes" (literally cave-dwellers) where the Hebrew names the Sukkiim.
notes.12:7: The Greek verb rendered "felt shame" (also in v. 12) conveys remorseful humility, and "drip down" reflects a distinctive Greek metaphor for wrath being poured out. The Greek also omits the Hebrew phrase "by the hand of Shishak" at the end of the verse.
notes.12:10: Unlike the Hebrew, where Rehoboam entrusts the bronze shields to the captains of the guards, the Greek states that Shishak appointed captains of the runners over him. Verse 11 similarly diverges in naming three groups entering the temple.
notes.12:16: The Greek text repeats "and was buried," reading both "was buried with his fathers" (Heb. slept with his fathers) and "was buried in the city of David."
notes.13:1: The Greek text reads "over Israel" where the Hebrew has "over Judah."
notes.13:2: The Greek reads "Maacah" (matching 11:20, against Heb. Micaiah) and "from Gibeon" (against Heb. Gibeah).
notes.13:4: The Greek names the mountain "Somoron" (a form elsewhere associated with Samaria) where the Hebrew has Zemaraim. In v. 5, the Greek likewise reads "a king" rather than the Hebrew "kingship."
notes.13:12: The Greek text omits the negative "do not" before "you will fight" (present in other Greek manuscripts and the Hebrew), and reads "over us" and "our fathers" where the Hebrew has "against you" and "your fathers."
notes.13:19: The Greek reads "Cana" where the Hebrew has Jeshanah.
notes.14:5: The Greek text lacks a verb before 'fortified cities in the land of Judah' (where the Hebrew and some other witnesses read 'and he built fortified cities'), leaving a verbless clause following verse 4.
notes.14:6: The Greek reads 'we will have dominion before the land' and 'He sought us out,' differing from the Hebrew ('the land is still before us; we have sought him'), and keeps 'and granted us success' inside Asa's speech.
notes.14:8: The Greek gives Zerah's force simply as 'thousands' (rather than a million, as in the Hebrew; compare also 'two hundred and fifty thousand' in v. 7 vs. 280,000 in Hebrew) and spells the destination 'Marisel,' distinct from 'Mareshah' in v. 9 (where the Greek also reads 'to the north of Mareshah' rather than 'Zephathah at Mareshah').
notes.14:12: The Greek reads 'Gedor' (also in v. 13) where the Hebrew text has 'Gerar.'
notes.14:14: The Greek uniquely identifies the object of attack alongside 'the tents of possessions' as the masculine group 'the Amazoneis,' a Septuagint-distinct name not found in the Hebrew text.
notes.15:2: The Greek shifts to the first-person plural 'while we are with Him' and omits the direct address to Asa found in the Hebrew text.
notes.15:3: In the Greek, verses 3-6 omit 'without a teaching priest' and frame Azariah's words in present and future tenses ('He will turn them back... there is no peace... nation will fight') rather than as past history.
notes.15:8: The Greek gives the prophet's name here as 'Adad' (distinct from 'Oded' in v. 1) and reads 'the temple of the Lord' where the Hebrew has 'the vestibule of the Lord.'
notes.15:16: Rather than removing Maacah from being queen mother for making an Asherah image (as in the Hebrew), the Greek reads that he removed her 'from ministering to Astarte,' using the distinct Greek divine name Astarte.
